title.en: Volume 1 Annals 1: Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 1

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝諱道成，字紹伯，姓蕭氏，小諱鬬將，漢相國蕭何二十四世孫也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, High Emperor, taboo name Daocheng, style name Shaobo, surname Xiao, childhood taboo Doujiang, was the twenty-fourth-generation descendant of Xiao He, Chancellor of State of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao, canonically titled Grand Progenitor, bore the name Daocheng and the style Shaobo; his clan was Xiao, and in childhood he was called Doujiang. He was the twenty-fourth in descent from Xiao He, Chancellor of State of Han.

sentences.zh: 何子酇定侯延生侍中彪，彪生公府掾章，章生皓，皓生仰，仰生御史大夫望之，望之生光祿大夫育，育生御史中丞紹，紹生光祿勳閎，閎生濟陰太守闡，闡生吳郡太守永，永生中山相苞，苞生博士周，周生蛇丘長矯，矯生州從事逵，逵生孝廉休，休生廣陵府丞豹，豹生太中大夫裔，裔生淮陰令整，整生即丘令儁，儁生輔國參軍樂子，宋昇明二年九月贈太常，生皇考。

translations.literal: Xiao He's son Yan, Marquis of Ding of Zan, begot Palace Attendant Biao; Biao begot Grand Secretariat Aide Zhang; Zhang begot Hao; Hao begot Yang; Yang begot Censor-in-Chief Wangzhi; Wangzhi begot Household Minister Yu; Yu begot Imperial Secretary Shao; Shao begot Director of the Imperial Secretariat Hong; Hong begot Administrator of Jiyin Chan; Chan begot Administrator of Wu Commandery Yong; Yong begot Chancellor of Zhongshan Bao; Bao begot Erudite Zhou; Zhou begot Chief of Sheqiu Jiao; Jiao begot Provincial Attendant Kui; Kui begot Filial and Incorrupt Xiu; Xiu begot Aide of the Guangling Commandery Bao; Bao begot Grand Master of Palace Counsel Yi; Yi begot Magistrate of Huaiyin Zheng; Zheng begot Magistrate of Jiuqiu Jun; Jun begot Staff Officer for Assisting the State Yuezi, posthumously made Grand Minister of Ceremonies in the ninth month of the second year of Shengming of Song, who begot the Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He's son Yan, Marquis of Ding of Zan, fathered Palace Attendant Biao; from Biao the line ran through a grand secretariat aide named Zhang, then Hao, Yang, the censor-in-chief Wangzhi, the household minister Yu, the imperial secretary Shao, the director of the imperial secretariat Hong, the administrator of Jiyin Chan, the administrator of Wu Yong, the chancellor of Zhongshan Bao, the erudite Zhou, the chief of Sheqiu Jiao, the provincial attendant Kui, the filial and incorrupt Xiu, a Guangling commandery aide Bao, the grand master of palace counsel Yi, the magistrate of Huaiyin Zheng, the magistrate of Jiuqiu Jun, and the staff officer for assisting the state Yuezi—posthumously raised to Grand Minister of Ceremonies in the ninth month of Song's second Shengming year—who fathered the Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 蕭何居沛，侍中彪免官居東海蘭陵縣中都鄉中都里。

translations.literal: Xiao He dwelt in Pei; Palace Attendant Biao, dismissed from office, dwelt in Zhongdu village, Zhongdu township, Lanling county, Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He had lived in Pei; after Palace Attendant Biao was dismissed, he settled in Zhongdu village, Zhongdu township, Lanling county in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 晉元康元年，分東海為蘭陵郡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuankang of Jin, Donghai was divided to form Lanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's first Yuankang year, Donghai was split off to form Lanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 中朝亂，淮陰令整字公齊，過江居晉陵武進縣之東城里。

translations.literal: When the central dynasty fell into turmoil, Magistrate of Huaiyin Zheng, styled Gongqi, crossed the river and dwelt in the Eastern City ward of Wujin county, Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the central court, Huaiyin's magistrate Zheng, styled Gongqi, crossed the Yangtze and settled in the Eastern City ward of Wujin in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 寓居江左者，皆僑置本土，加以南名，於是為南蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Those dwelling east of the river all had their native lands registered in exile districts with the prefix "Southern" added; thus they became natives of Lanling in Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Émigrés south of the Yangtze had their home districts registered in exile prefectures with "Southern" prefixed to the name; thus the clan became natives of Lanling in Southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 皇考諱承之，字嗣伯。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father taboo Chengzhi, style name Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father bore the name Chengzhi and the style Sibo.

sentences.zh: 少有大志，才力過人，宗人丹陽尹摹之、北兖州刺史源之竝見知重。

translations.literal: In youth he cherished great resolve; his talent and strength surpassed others; his clansmen, Administrator of Danyang Mu Zhi and Inspector of North Yanzhou Yuanzhi, both held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he nursed great ambition, and his talent and force outstripped other men. His kinsmen Mu Zhi, administrator of Danyang, and Yuanzhi, inspector of North Yanzhou, both marked him for trust.

sentences.zh: 初為建威府參軍，義熙中，蜀賊譙縱初平，皇考遷揚武將軍、安固汶山二郡太守，善於綏撫。

translations.literal: At first he served as staff officer in the Establishing Might Office; in the Yixi era, when the Shu bandit Qiao Zong was first pacified, the Imperial Father was transferred to General Who Raises Martial Might and Administrator of the two commanderies of Angu and Wenshan, skilled at soothing and settling.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the staff of the Establishing Might office. In the Yixi era, when the Shu rebel Qiao Zong was newly subdued, the Imperial Father was made General Who Raises Martial Might and administrator of Angu and Wenshan, and proved adept at pacification.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，徙為威烈將軍、濟南太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was transferred to General Who Establishes Martial Glory and Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanjia reign he was transferred to General Who Establishes Martial Glory and made administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 七年，右將軍到彥之北伐大敗，虜乘勝破青部諸郡國，別帥安平公乙旃眷寇濟南，皇考率數百人拒戰，退之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Right General Dao Yanzhi suffered great defeat on the northern campaign; the enemy took advantage of victory to break the commanderies and principalities of Qing Province; a separate commander, the Duke of Ping'an Yizhan Juan, raided Jinan; the Imperial Father led several hundred men to resist and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Right General Dao Yanzhi was routed on the northern expedition. The enemy pressed the victory, overrunning the commanderies of Qing, while a detached force under the Duke of Ping'an, Yizhan Juan, struck at Jinan. The Imperial Father led several hundred men to meet them and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 虜眾大集，皇考使偃兵開城門。

translations.literal: The enemy masses gathered in strength; the Imperial Father had the troops lay down their arms and opened the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy host massed in strength, the Imperial Father ordered his men to stand down and opened the city gates.

sentences.zh: 眾諫曰：「賊眾我寡，何輕敵之甚！

translations.literal: The crowd remonstrated, saying: "The bandits are many and we are few—why treat the enemy so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers protested: "The enemy outnumber us—why show them such contempt?"

sentences.zh: 」皇考曰：「今日懸守窮城，事已危急，若復示弱，必為所屠，惟當見彊待之耳。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father said: "Today we hang on defense in a desperate city; affairs are already critical; if we show weakness again, we shall surely be slaughtered—one must only meet them with a show of strength."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father said, "We cling to a doomed city on a hair trigger. If we show fear again, they will cut us down. We must meet them as though we were the stronger."

sentences.zh: 」虜疑有伏兵，遂引去。

translations.literal: The enemy suspected an ambush and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suspected a trap and drew off.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭思話欲委鎮保險，皇考固諫不從，思話失據潰走。

translations.literal: Qing Province Inspector Xiao Sihua wished to abandon the prefecture and hold the defiles; the Imperial Father firmly remonstrated but was not obeyed; Sihua lost his footing and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's inspector Xiao Sihua meant to abandon his seat and cling to mountain strongholds. The Imperial Father argued against it in vain; Sihua lost his footing and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 明年，征南大將軍檀道濟於壽張轉戰班師，滑臺陷沒，兖州刺史竺靈秀抵罪。

translations.literal: The next year, Grand General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji turned from battle at Shouzhang and marched back; Huatai fell; Yanzhou Inspector Zhu Lingxiu was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Grand General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji broke off fighting at Shouzhang and marched home; Huatai was lost, and Yanzhou's inspector Zhu Lingxiu was called to account.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝以皇考有全城之功，手書與都督長沙王義欣曰：「承之理民直亦不在武幹後，今擬為兖州，□□檀征南詳之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song, because the Imperial Father had the merit of preserving the whole city, wrote in his own hand to the commander-in-chief, Prince of Changsha Yixin, saying: "Chengzhi in governing the people is straightforward and not behind in martial capacity; he is now proposed for Yanzhou—[lacuna] let Grand General Who Conquers the South Tan deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song, crediting the Imperial Father with saving the city intact, wrote in his own hand to the commander-in-chief, Prince Yixin of Changsha: "Chengzhi governs with integrity and is no laggard in martial affairs. I propose him for Yanzhou—[text lost]—let Grand General Tan Daoji advise."

sentences.zh: 」皇考與道濟無素故，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father had no prior tie with Daoji; the matter therefore lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father had no old connection with Tan Daoji, and the appointment came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷輔國鎮北中兵參軍、員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Corps Commander of the Assisting State and Pacifying North Army and to outer court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to central corps commander of the Assisting State and Pacifying North armies and to outer court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 十年，蕭思話為梁州刺史，皇考為其橫野府司馬、漢中太守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xiao Sihua became Inspector of Liang Province; the Imperial Father was his Wild Expansion Office marshal and Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xiao Sihua became inspector of Liang, and the Imperial Father served as his Wild Expansion army marshal and administrator of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 氐帥楊難當寇漢川，梁州刺史甄法護棄城走，思話至襄陽不進，皇考輕軍前行，攻氐偽魏興太守薛健於黃金山，剋之。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Nandang raided Han River country; Liang Inspector Zhen Fahu abandoned the city and fled; Sihua reached Xiangyang but did not advance; the Imperial Father led a light column forward and attacked the Di puppet Administrator of Weixing Xue Jian at Golden Mountain, taking him.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Nandang raided the Han basin. Liang's inspector Zhen Fahu abandoned his city and fled; Sihua halted at Xiangyang and would not advance. The Imperial Father pushed ahead with a light column, attacked the Di puppet administrator of Weixing, Xue Jian, at Golden Mountain, and took him.

sentences.zh: 黃金山，張魯舊戍，南接漢川，北枕驛道，險固之極。

translations.literal: Golden Mountain was an old garrison of Zhang Lu, south joining Han River country, north resting on the post road—of extreme strategic strength.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Mountain had been Zhang Lu's old stronghold, joining the Han country to the south and commanding the post road to the north—ground of the utmost strength.

sentences.zh: 健既潰散，皇考即據之。

translations.literal: When Jian had already been routed and scattered, the Imperial Father at once seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jian's force was broken, the Imperial Father seized the height at once.

sentences.zh: 氐偽梁、秦二州刺史趙溫先據州城，聞皇考至，退據小城，薛健退屯下桃城，立柴營，皇考引軍與對壘，相去二里。

translations.literal: The Di puppet Inspectors of Liang and Qin, Zhao Wen, had first held the provincial city; hearing the Imperial Father had come, he withdrew to a lesser city; Xue Jian withdrew to encamp at Xiatao city and raised stockade camps; the Imperial Father led his army to face them across a distance of two li.
translations.idiomatic: The Di puppet inspectors of Liang and Qin, Zhao Wen, already held the provincial seat; when he heard the Imperial Father was coming, he fell back to a lesser city. Xue Jian withdrew to Xiatao and threw up stockades. The Imperial Father drew up facing them two li away.

sentences.zh: 健與偽馮翊太守蒲

translations.literal: Jian and the puppet Administrator of Fufeng Pu
translations.idiomatic: Jian and the puppet administrator of Fufeng, Pu

translations.literal: (Han)
translations.idiomatic: —Han—

sentences.zh: 〔早〕子悉力出戰，皇考大破之，健等閉營自守不敢出，思話繼至，賊乃稍退。

translations.literal: [Zao]zi exerted their full strength in battle; the Imperial Father inflicted a great defeat; Jian and the others shut their camps and dared not come out; Sihua followed after, and the bandits then gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: [Zao]'s son threw everything into the fight; the Imperial Father broke them utterly. Jian and his men shut themselves in camp and dared not stir; Sihua came up behind, and the enemy at last drew off.

sentences.zh: 皇考進至峨公山，為左衞將軍、沙州刺史呂平大眾所圍積日，建武將軍蕭汪之、平西督護段虯等至，表裏奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father advanced to Mount E'gong, was besieged for many days by the great host of Lü Ping, Left Guards General and Inspector of Shazhou; the Establishing Martial General Xiao Wangzhi, the Pacifying West staff commander Duan Jiu, and others arrived; attacking from within and without with combined force, they inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father pushed on to Mount E'gong and was hemmed in for days by the great host of Lü Ping, Left Guards general and inspector of Shazhou. When the Establishing Martial general Xiao Wangzhi and the Pacifying West staff commander Duan Jiu came up, they struck from within and without and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 難當又遣息和領步騎萬餘人，夾漢水兩岸，援趙溫，攻逼皇考。

translations.literal: Nandang also sent his son He at the head of more than ten thousand foot and horse on both banks of the Han as reinforcements for Zhao Wen, pressing the attack on the Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang also sent his son He with more than ten thousand foot and horse along both banks of the Han to reinforce Zhao Wen and press the Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 相拒四十餘日。

translations.literal: They faced one another for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides stood off for more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 賊皆衣犀甲，刀箭不能傷。

translations.literal: The bandits all wore rhinoceros-hide armor; blades and arrows could not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy all wore rhinoceros-hide armor against which blade and arrow could not bite.

sentences.zh: 皇考命軍中斷槊長數尺，以大斧搥其後，賊不能當，乃焚營退。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father ordered the army to cut spears several chi long and drive them in with great axes from behind; the bandits could not withstand it and therefore burned their camps and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father ordered spears cut several chi long and driven home with great axes from behind; the enemy could not stand before them, burned their camps, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇考追至南城，眾軍自後而進，連戰皆捷，梁州平。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father pursued to Nancheng; the mass of armies came up from behind and joined battle in succession, all victorious; Liang Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Father pursued to Nancheng. The main columns came up from behind and fought in succession, winning every engagement, and Liang Province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「承之稟命先驅，蒙險深入，全軍屢剋，奮其忠果，可龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Chengzhi received the mandate as vanguard, braved peril and went deep, repeatedly overcame with the whole army, and displayed loyal valor—he may be made General of Dragon Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Chengzhi, taking the mandate as vanguard, braved peril in deep country, and with the whole army won again and again, showing loyal valor—let him be made General of Dragon Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 」隨府轉寧朔司馬，太守如故。

translations.literal: He followed the establishment in transfer to Pacifying the North army marshal; his post as administrator was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the establishment in transfer to marshal of the Pacifying North army while retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 入為太子屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Colonel of Rapid Cavalry for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Colonel of Rapid Cavalry on the heir apparent's staff.

sentences.zh: 文帝以平氐之勞，青州缺，將欲授用。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because of the merit in pacifying the Di, with Qingzhou vacant intended to appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, honoring the Di campaign, meant to give him the vacant Qingzhou post.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康秉政，皇考不附，乃轉為江夏王司徒中兵參軍、龍驤將軍、南泰山太守，封晉興縣五等男，邑三百四十戶。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang held the government; the Imperial Father would not attach himself to him; he was therefore transferred to central corps commander on the Prince of Jiangxia's staff as Grand Minister of Education, General of Dragon Cavalry, Administrator of South Taishan, enfeoffed as fifth-grade baron of Jinxing with a fief of three hundred forty households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held the government, and the Imperial Father would not join his faction; he was therefore shifted to central corps commander on Prince Jiangxia's staff as grand minister of education, made General of Dragon Cavalry and administrator of South Taishan, and enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jinxing with three hundred forty households.

sentences.zh: 遷右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年殂，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 梁土民思之，於峨公山立廟祭祀。

translations.literal: The people of Liang land missed him; on Mount E'gong they raised a temple to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liang longed for him; on Mount E'gong they raised a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Household Minister with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Shengming year he was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Household Minister with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 太祖以元嘉四年丁卯歲生。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng was born in the fourth year of Yuanjia, the year dingmao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng was born in the fourth year of Yuanjia, the cyclical year dingmao.

sentences.zh: 姿表英異，龍顙鍾聲，鱗文遍體。

translations.literal: His bearing and appearance were outstanding; dragon forehead and bell-like voice; scale patterns covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was striking, with a dragon's brow and a bell's resonance; scale-like markings covered his body.

sentences.zh: 儒士雷次宗立學於鷄籠山，太祖年十三，受業，治禮及左氏春秋。

translations.literal: The scholar Lei Cizong established a school on Cock Cage Mountain; Xiao Daocheng at age thirteen received instruction, studying ritual and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar Lei Cizong founded a school on Cock Cage Mountain; at thirteen Xiao Daocheng took instruction there in ritual and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 十七年，宋大將軍彭城王義康被黜，鎮豫章，皇考領兵防守，太祖舍業南行。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Song Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, was deposed; he garrisoned Yuzhang; the Imperial Father led troops to defend; Xiao Daocheng abandoned his studies and went south.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Song grand general, Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, was deposed and garrisoned Yuzhang; the Imperial Father led troops to hold the line, and Xiao Daocheng left his studies to go south.

sentences.zh: 十九年，竟陵蠻動，文帝遣太祖領偏軍討沔北蠻。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the Jingling barbarians stirred; Emperor Wen sent Xiao Daocheng at the head of a detached army to attack the barbarians north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Jingling tribes rose; Emperor Wen sent Xiao Daocheng with a detached force against the barbarians north of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，伐索虜，至丘檻山，竝破走。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, campaigning against the Northern Wei, reaching Mount Qiujian, he together defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, on campaign against the Northern Wei, he reached Mount Qiujian and together routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，雍州刺史蕭思話鎮襄陽，啟太祖自隨，戍沔北，討樊、鄧諸山蠻，破其聚落。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Yong Province Inspector Xiao Sihua garrisoned Xiangyang and requested that Xiao Daocheng follow him; he garrisoned north of the Mian, attacked the mountain barbarians of Fan and Deng, and broke their settlements.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Yong's inspector Xiao Sihua held Xiangyang and asked that Xiao Daocheng accompany him; he garrisoned north of the Mian, struck the mountain barbarians of Fan and Deng, and destroyed their settlements.

sentences.zh: 初為左軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: At first he served as Central Troop Commander in the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: His first post was as central corps commander on the Left Army staff.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，索虜圍汝南戍主陳憲，臺遣寧朔將軍臧質、安蠻司馬劉康祖救之，文帝使太祖宣旨，授節度。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Northern Wei besieged Chen Xian, garrison commander of Runan; the court dispatched General Who Pacifies the North Zang Zhi and Chief of Staff for Pacifying the Barbarians Liu Kangzu to rescue him; Emperor Wen sent Xiao Daocheng to proclaim the imperial will and grant overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, the Wei laid siege to Chen Xian at the Runan garrison. The court sent Zang Zhi, General Who Pacifies the North, and Liu Kangzu, chief of staff for the Pacification of the Barbarians, to relieve him. Emperor Wen dispatched Xiao Daocheng to deliver the imperial instructions and invest him with operational authority.

sentences.zh: 聞虜主拓跋燾向彭城，質等回軍救援，至盱眙，太祖與質別軍主胡宗之等五軍，步騎數千人前驅，燾已潛過淮，卒相遇於莞山下，合戰敗績，緣淮奔退，宗之等皆陷沒。

translations.literal: Hearing that the enemy ruler Tuoba Tao was marching on Pengcheng, Zhi and the others turned the army to rescue; reaching Xuyi, Xiao Daocheng with Zhi's detached army commanders Hu Zongzhi and others—five armies, several thousand infantry and cavalry in the vanguard—Tao had already secretly crossed the Huai; they suddenly met at Mount Guan, joined battle and were defeated, fled along the Huai in retreat, and Zongzhi and the others were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the Wei emperor Tuoba Tao was bearing down on Pengcheng, Zang Zhi and his force wheeled about to relieve the city. At Xuyi, Xiao Daocheng, with Zang Zhi's detached commanders Hu Zongzhi and others—five armies, several thousand foot and horse in the van—found that Tao had already stolen across the Huai. They clashed without warning below Mount Guan, were routed, and fled along the river; Zongzhi and his fellows were swallowed up.

sentences.zh: 太祖還就質固守，為虜所攻圍，甚危急，事寧，還京師。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng returned to join Zhi in stubborn defense, was besieged by the enemy, in extreme peril; when affairs were settled, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng fell back to hold the line with Zang Zhi. The enemy hemmed them in and the danger was acute; when the crisis passed, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，領偏軍征仇池。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he led a detached army to campaign against Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he took command of a detached force and marched against Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 梁州西界舊有武興戍，晉隆安中沒屬氐；

translations.literal: On Liang Province's western border there had long been the Wuxing garrison; in the Long'an era of Jin it was lost and came under the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Province's western marches had long held the Wuxing garrison, but in Jin's Long'an era it fell to the Di.

sentences.zh: 武興西北有蘭皋戍，去仇池二百里。

translations.literal: Northwest of Wuxing was the Langao garrison, two hundred li from Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Wuxing stood the Langao garrison, two hundred li from Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 太祖擊二壘，皆破之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng attacked both fortresses and broke them both.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng stormed both strongholds and took them.

sentences.zh: 遂從谷口入關，未至長安八十里，梁州刺史劉秀之遣司馬馬注助太祖攻談堤城，拔之，虜偽河閒公奔走。

translations.literal: Then he entered the pass from Gukou; when still eighty li from Chang'an, Liang Province Inspector Liu Xiuzhi sent his army marshal Ma Zhu to assist Xiao Daocheng in attacking Tandi city; they took it, and the enemy's false Prince of Hejian fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered the pass by Gukou. Still eighty li short of Chang'an, Liang Province inspector Liu Xiuzhi sent his marshal Ma Zhu to help Xiao Daocheng take Tandi; the city fell, and the Wei puppet Prince of Hejian ran.

sentences.zh: 虜救兵至，太祖軍力疲少，又聞文帝崩，乃燒城還南鄭。

translations.literal: Enemy relief troops arrived; Xiao Daocheng's army was weary and few; hearing also that Emperor Wen had died, he burned the city and returned to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reinforcements arrived while Xiao Daocheng's men were spent and few. When he heard that Emperor Wen had died, he fired the city and withdrew to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 襲爵晉興縣五等男。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank of fifth-grade baron of Jinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the fifth-rank barony of Jinxing County.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，除江夏王大司馬參軍，隨府轉太宰，遷員外郎、直閤中書舍人、西

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaojian era, he was appointed staff officer to the Grand Marshal of the Prince of Jiangxia; when the establishment transferred to Grand Preceptor, he was promoted to outer gentleman, attendant of the Direct Access Office and palace scribe, and [staff officer to the Prince of] Western
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojian reign he was named staff officer to the Prince of Jiangxia's grand marshal; when that household became the Grand Preceptor's establishment he went with it, rising to outer court gentleman, attendant in the Direct Access Office, and aide to the Prince of Western

translations.literal: (Ling)
translations.idiomatic: —Ling—

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕王撫軍參軍、建康令。

translations.literal: [Yang] King's military staff officer and magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: [Yang], as military aide on the prince's staff and magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 新安王子鸞有盛寵，簡選僚佐，為北

translations.literal: The Prince of Xin'an, Ziluan, enjoyed extraordinary favor; when selecting staff, [Xiao Daocheng] was made Northern
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an stood in the emperor's highest favor; when the prince chose his staff, Xiao Daocheng was appointed to the Northern

translations.literal: (Army)
translations.idiomatic: Army

sentences.zh: 中郎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Army central corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Army post of central corps commander.

sentences.zh: 陳太后憂，起為武烈將軍，復為建康令，中兵如故。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Chen's mourning began, he was recalled to serve as General Who Establishes Martial Glory; he again became magistrate of Jiankang, his central corps command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of mourning for Empress Dowager Chen he was recalled as General Who Establishes Martial Glory, again made magistrate of Jiankang while retaining his central corps command.

sentences.zh: 景和世，除後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era he was appointed General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinghe reign he was made General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 值明帝立，為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, he became General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was promoted to General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 時四方反叛，會稽太守尋陽王子房及東諸郡皆起兵，明帝加太祖輔國將軍，率眾東討。

translations.literal: At that time the four quarters rebelled; the Administrator of Kuaiji, the Prince of Xunyang Zifang, and the eastern commanderies all raised troops; Emperor Ming added to Xiao Daocheng the title General Who Assists the State and sent him east at the head of an army to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion flared on every side. Kuaiji's administrator, Prince Zifang of Xunyang, and the eastern prefectures all took up arms. Emperor Ming gave Xiao Daocheng the rank of General Who Assists the State and sent him east to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至晉陵，與賊前鋒將程捍、孫曇瓘等戰，一日破賊十二壘。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinling, he fought the rebels' vanguard generals Cheng Han, Sun Tanwan, and others; in a single day he broke twelve of the enemy camps.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling he met the rebel van under Cheng Han, Sun Tanwan, and others and in one day shattered twelve encampments.

sentences.zh: 分軍定諸縣，晉陵太守袁摽棄城走，東境諸城相繼奔散。

translations.literal: He divided his force to secure the counties; Jinling Administrator Yuan Biao abandoned the city and fled, and the eastern prefectures' cities surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He detached columns to pacify the counties. Jinling's administrator Yuan Biao fled his city, and stronghold after stronghold in the east gave way.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史薛安都反彭城，從子索兒寇淮陰，山陽太守程天祚舉城叛，徐州刺史申令孫又降，徵太祖討之。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu rebelled at Pengcheng; his nephew Suo'er raided Huaiyin; Shanyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo rose in the city; Xuzhou Inspector Shen Ling sun also surrendered; Xiao Daocheng was summoned to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu revolted at Pengcheng. His nephew Suo'er struck at Huaiyin; Shanyang's administrator Cheng Tianzuo turned his city; inspector Shen Lingsun of Xuzhou also went over. Xiao Daocheng was called up to crush them.

sentences.zh: 時太祖平東賊還，又將南討，出次新亭，前軍已發，而索兒自睢陵渡淮，馬步萬餘人，擊殺臺軍主孫耿，縱兵逼前軍張永營，告急。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Daocheng had just pacified the eastern rebels and was about to march south again; he encamped at Xinting, the vanguard already on the road, when Suo'er crossed the Huai from Suiling with more than ten thousand horse and foot, killed the court army commander Sun Geng, and drove his troops against the vanguard Zhang Yong's camp, sending urgent word for help.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng had barely finished in the east and was turning south when he halted at Xinting. His vanguard was already abroad, but Suo'er forded the Huai at Suiling with ten thousand-odd horse and foot, killed the court commander Sun Geng, and pressed Zhang Yong's forward camp, crying for relief.

sentences.zh: 明帝聞賊渡，遽追太祖往救之，屯破釜。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, hearing that the bandits had crossed, urgently recalled Xiao Daocheng to rescue them; he encamped at Pofu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming learned the enemy had crossed the river, he rushed Xiao Daocheng to the rescue. Xiao Daocheng took station at Pofu.

sentences.zh: 索兒向鍾離，永遣寧朔將軍王寬據盱眙，遏其歸路。

translations.literal: Suo'er moved on Zhongli; Yong sent General Who Pacifies the North Wang Kuan to hold Xuyi and block his line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er bore down on Zhongli. Zhang Yong posted Wang Kuan, General Who Pacifies the North, at Xuyi to cut off his retreat.

sentences.zh: 索兒擊破臺軍主高道慶，走之於石鼈，將西歸。

translations.literal: Suo'er defeated the court army commander Gao Daoqing, drove him to Shibie, and was about to turn west.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er broke the court officer Gao Daoqing and chased him to Shibie, then prepared to march west.

sentences.zh: 王寬與軍主任農夫先據白鵠澗，張永遣太祖馳督寬，索兒東要擊太祖，使不得前。

translations.literal: Wang Kuan and the army commander Ren Nongfu first seized Baihe Stream; Zhang Yong sent Xiao Daocheng at full gallop to oversee Kuan; Suo'er moved east to intercept Xiao Daocheng and keep him from advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuan and the army commander Ren Nongfu seized Baihe Stream first. Zhang Yong sent Xiao Daocheng at the double to supervise Kuan, but Suo'er swung east to bar his path.

sentences.zh: 太祖鼓行結陣，直入寬壘，索兒望見不敢發。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng beat the drums, formed ranks, and marched straight into Kuan's camp; Suo'er saw him and did not dare strike.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng beat the drums, dressed his lines, and marched straight into Kuan's camp. Suo'er looked on and did not dare engage.

sentences.zh: 經數日，索兒引軍頓石梁，太祖追之至葛冢，候騎還云賊至，太祖乃頓軍引管，分兩馬軍夾營外以待之。

translations.literal: After several days Suo'er drew up at Shiliang; Xiao Daocheng pursued him to Gezhong; scouts returned saying the bandits had come; Xiao Daocheng then halted the army and took command, dividing two horse units to wait outside the camp on either flank.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Suo'er halted at Shiliang. Xiao Daocheng followed him to Gezhong. When scouts reported the enemy at hand, he halted, took the command in hand, and split two cavalry wings to lie in wait beyond the camp.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，賊馬步奄至，又推火車數道攻戰。

translations.literal: In a little while the enemy's horse and foot closed in together, and they also pushed several lanes of fire-wagons into the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the rebel horse and foot swarmed in, rolling several lines of fire-carts into the battle.

sentences.zh: 相持移日，乃出輕兵攻賊西，使馬軍合擊其後，賊眾大敗，追奔獲其器仗。

translations.literal: They grappled for a long while; then he sent light troops against the enemy's west wing and had the cavalry strike from the rear; the rebel masses were utterly defeated, and in the pursuit their weapons and gear were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The fight wore on until he sent light troops against their western wing and ordered the horse to close on their rear. The rebel host broke; the pursuit heaped up their arms and baggage.

sentences.zh: 進屯石梁澗北。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped north of Shiliang Stream.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward and camped north of Shiliang Stream.

sentences.zh: 索兒夜遣千人來斫營，營中驚，太祖臥不起，宣令左右案部不得動，須臾賊散。

translations.literal: Suo'er sent a thousand men by night to cut the camp; the camp was alarmed; Xiao Daocheng lay and did not rise, ordering those at his side to hold their posts and not move; in a moment the bandits dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er sent a thousand men to raid the camp by night. The lines erupted in alarm, but Xiao Daocheng lay still and gave orders that none should stir from his post; presently the raiders melted away.

sentences.zh: 太祖議欲於石梁西南高地築壘通南道，斷賊走路，索兒果來爭之，太祖率軍擊破之，賊馬自相踐藉死。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng proposed building a fort on the high ground southwest of Shiliang to open a southern road and cut the bandits' escape; Suo'er came as expected to contest it; Xiao Daocheng led the army and broke them, and the enemy horses trampled one another to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng planned a fort on the heights southwest of Shiliang to open a road south and sever the enemy's retreat. Suo'er came to dispute the ground as foreseen; Xiao Daocheng led his men and broke him, and the rebel horses stampeded each other to death.

sentences.zh: 索兒走向鍾離，太祖追至黯黮而還。

translations.literal: Suo'er fled toward Zhongli; Xiao Daocheng pursued to the gloaming and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er fled toward Zhongli. Xiao Daocheng chased until dark and turned back.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，封西陽縣侯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Rapid Cavalry, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiyang County with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Rapid Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiyang, with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷巴陵王衞軍司馬，隨鎮會稽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to army marshal of the Prince of Baling's Guard Army and followed the prince in garrison at Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to army marshal on the Prince of Baling's guard staff and went with the prince to garrison Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史晉安王子勛遣臨川內史張淹自鄱陽嶠道入三吳，臺軍主沈思仁與偽龍驤將軍任皇、鎮西參軍劉越緒各據險相守。

translations.literal: Jiang Province Inspector, the Prince of Jin'an Zixun, sent Linchuan Interior Administrator Zhang Yan by the Poyang ridge road into the Three Wu; the court army commander Shen Siren and the false Dragon Rapid General Ren Huang and the false Western Campaign Staff Officer Liu Yuexu each held hazardous ground and faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Province inspector Prince Zixun of Jin'an sent Linchuan's interior administrator Zhang Yan over the Poyang ridge into the Three Wu. The court commander Shen Siren and the rebel generals Ren Huang and Liu Yuexu each held defiles and stood off.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣太祖領三千人討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Xiao Daocheng at the head of three thousand men to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming dispatched Xiao Daocheng with three thousand men to bring them to battle.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷器甲皆充南討，太祖軍容寡闕，乃編椶皮為馬具裝，析竹為寄生，夜舉火進軍，賊望見恐懼，未戰而走。

translations.literal: At that time the court's armor and weapons had all been committed to the southern campaign; Xiao Daocheng's army was scantily equipped; he therefore plaited palm bark into horse trappings and split bamboo into horse screens; by night he advanced with torches raised, and the bandits, seeing them, were afraid and fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The court's arms had all gone south, and Xiao Daocheng's column was thinly equipped. He plaited palm bark into horse armor, cut bamboo for cavalry screens, and marched by night with torches lifted. The enemy took fright at the sight and ran before a blow was struck.

sentences.zh: 還除桂陽王征北司馬、南東海太守、行南徐州事。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed army marshal on the Prince of Guiyang's northern campaign staff, Administrator of Southern Donghai, and acting Xuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he was made army marshal on Prince Guiyang's northern campaign staff, administrator of Southern Donghai, and acting inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，明帝遣張永、沈攸之以眾喻降薛安都，謂太祖曰：「吾今因此北討，卿意以為何如？

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Ming had sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a host to induce Xue Andu to surrender, and said to Xiao Daocheng: "I now mean to use this occasion for a northern campaign—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Ming had sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a large force to win Xue Andu over by persuasion. He asked Xiao Daocheng, "I intend to turn this into a northern expedition—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖對曰：「安都才識不足，狡猾有餘。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng replied: "Andu lacks talent and insight but has cunning in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng answered, "Andu is short on ability and judgment but long on guile.

sentences.zh: 若長轡緩御，則必遣子入朝；

translations.literal: If you hold the reins long and drive gently, he will surely send his son to court;
translations.idiomatic: Hold the reins long and drive gently, and he is sure to send his son to court;

sentences.zh: 今以兵逼之，彼將懼而為計，恐非國之利也。

translations.literal: now, if you press him with troops, he will fear and contrive a plan— I fear it will not profit the state."
translations.idiomatic: but press him now with an army and fear will drive him to scheme. I doubt that will serve the realm."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「眾軍猛銳，何往不剋。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The mass of our armies is fierce and keen—where would they not conquer?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Our hosts are fierce and sharp—what place would they not take?

sentences.zh: 卿每杖策，幸勿多言。

translations.literal: You lean on your staff at every turn; pray do not say more."
translations.idiomatic: You lean on your staff and counsel at every turn; for once, say no more."

sentences.zh: 」安都見兵至，果引索虜，永等敗於彭城。

translations.literal: When Andu saw the army arrive, he indeed brought in the Northern Wei; Yong and the others were defeated at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu saw the army come, he did indeed call in the Wei. Zhang Yong and his fellows were broken at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 淮南孤弱，以太祖為假冠軍將軍、持節、都督北討前鋒諸軍事，鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: Huainan was isolated and weak; Xiao Daocheng was made Acting General Who Establishes the Champion, with credential staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of the Northern Campaign vanguard, and garrisoned at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: With Huainan left exposed and weak, the court made Xiao Daocheng Acting Champion General, gave him the staff of authority, and set him to command the northern vanguard from a base at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，沈攸之、吳喜北敗於睢口，諸城戍大小悉奔歸，虜遂

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi were defeated in the northern campaign at Suikou; garrisons great and small all fled homeward, and the barbarians then
translations.idiomatic: In the third Taishi year Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi were routed north of the Huai at Suikou; strongholds up and down the line abandoned their posts and fled, and the barbarians then

translations.literal: (retreated)
translations.idiomatic: —retreated—

sentences.zh: 〔進〕至淮北，圍角城，戍主賈法度力弱不敵。

translations.literal: [advanced] to north of the Huai, besieged Jiaocheng; the garrison commander Jia Fadu was too weak to resist.
translations.idiomatic: advanced to the north bank of the Huai and laid siege to Jiaocheng, whose commander Jia Fadu was too few to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 諸將勸太祖渡岸救之，太祖不許，遣軍主高道慶將數百張弩浮艦淮中，遙射城外虜，弩一發數百箭俱去，虜騎相引避之，乃命進戰，城圍即解。

translations.literal: The generals urged Xiao Daocheng to cross the shore and rescue them; he would not consent but sent the army commander Gao Daoqing with several hundred repeating crossbows on pontoon boats in the Huai, shooting at the barbarians outside the city from afar; one trigger of the crossbows loosed several hundred arrows at once, and the barbarian cavalry led one another in avoidance; then he ordered an advance into battle, and the siege was at once raised.
translations.idiomatic: His officers begged him to cross the river and relieve the town. He refused, but sent Gao Daoqing with hundreds of repeating crossbows on rafts midstream to rain bolts on the enemy outside the walls—one pull could send hundreds of shafts flying, and the barbarian horse drew back in chain. Only then did he order the assault, and the siege lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 遷督南兖徐二州諸軍事、南兖州刺史，持節、假冠軍、督北討如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of all military affairs of the two provinces of South Yanzhou and Xuzhou and Inspector of South Yanzhou, with credential staff, Acting Champion General, and Northern Campaign supervision unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervise the armies of South Yanzhou and Xuzhou and made inspector of South Yanzhou, retaining his staff, his acting champion rank, and his northern command.

sentences.zh: 五年，進督兖、青、冀三州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to supervise Yanzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his authority was extended over Yanzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，除黃門侍郎，領越騎校尉，不拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was offered the Yellow Gate and the colonelcy of the Valiant Cavalry; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 復授冠軍將軍，留本任。

translations.literal: He was again granted the title General Who Establishes the Champion and retained his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Champion General and kept his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 明帝常嫌太祖非人臣相，而民間流言，云「蕭道成當為天子」，明帝愈以為疑，遣冠軍將軍吳喜以三千人北使，令喜留軍破釜，自持銀壺酒封賜太祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming often suspected that Xiao Daocheng did not have the countenance of a subject; moreover popular rumor said, "Xiao Daocheng is destined to be Son of Heaven," and the emperor grew all the more suspicious. He sent the Champion General Wu Xi north on a mission with three thousand men, ordering Xi to leave the army at Pofu while he himself bore a sealed silver flask of wine to bestow on Xiao Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had long thought Xiao Daocheng's face was not that of a loyal minister, and when the streets began to murmur that "Xiao Daocheng will be Son of Heaven," his suspicion deepened. He dispatched Champion General Wu Xi north with three thousand men, told Xi to halt the army at Pofu, and came himself with a sealed silver flask of wine for Xiao Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖戎衣出門迎，即酌飲之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng in martial dress went out the gate to receive him and at once poured and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng met him at the gate in field dress, poured at once, and drank.

sentences.zh: 喜還，帝意乃悅。

translations.literal: When Xi returned, the emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi came back, the emperor was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 七年，徵還京師，部下勸勿就徵，太祖曰：「諸卿闇於見事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned back to the capital; his subordinates urged him not to answer the summons. Xiao Daocheng said, "You gentlemen are blind to how matters stand.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled to the capital. His officers urged him not to go. Xiao Daocheng said, "You do not see what is before you.

sentences.zh: 主上自誅諸弟，為太子稚弱，作萬歲後計，何關佗族。

translations.literal: The sovereign has himself killed his younger brothers; the heir is young and tender—they are making plans for the age to come. What has that to do with other clans?
translations.idiomatic: The throne has just slaughtered its own brothers; the crown prince is a child. They are laying plans for the long years ahead. What has any of that to do with our house?

sentences.zh: 惟應速發，事緩必見疑。

translations.literal: We should only set out quickly; if affairs drag, suspicion is sure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: We should go at once. Delay will only breed doubt.

sentences.zh: 今骨肉相害，自非靈長之運，禍難將興，方與卿等勠力耳。

translations.literal: Now that flesh and blood turn on one another, this is no fortune meant to last—calamity is about to rise. It is time to strive together with you all.
translations.idiomatic: When kin begin to devour kin, the mandate is already broken. Disaster is coming. Then we must stand together.

sentences.zh: 」拜散騎常侍、太子左衞率。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Palace Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 時世祖以功當別封贛縣，太祖以一門二封，固辭不受，詔許之。

translations.literal: At that time the future Emperor Wu merited a separate enfeoffment in Gan county; Xiao Daocheng, holding that one household with two enfeoffments was improper, firmly declined and would not accept; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wu had earned a separate fief in Gan county. Xiao Daocheng, saying one family could not hold two enfeoffments, refused firmly, and the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 加邑二百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred households were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遺詔為右衞將軍，領衞尉，加兵五百人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, the testamentary edict made him General of the Right Guard, acting Commandant of the Guard, with five hundred additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Ming's death the testament named him General of the Right Guard and acting Commandant of the Guard, with five hundred extra men.

sentences.zh: 與尚書令袁粲、護軍褚淵、領軍劉勔共掌機事。

translations.literal: Together with Secretariat Director Yuan Can, Protector of the Army Chu Yuan, and Army Director Liu Xu he jointly held the levers of power.
translations.idiomatic: He shared control of state affairs with Yuan Can, director of the Secretariat, Chu Yuan, Protector of the Army, and Liu Xu, Army Director.

sentences.zh: 又別領東北選事。

translations.literal: He also separately oversaw northeast selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also took charge of appointments in the northeast.

sentences.zh: 尋解衞尉，加侍中，領石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved of the commandantship, made Palace Attendant, and given charge of Stone City garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left the commandant's office, became Palace Attendant, and took command of the Stone City garrison.

sentences.zh: 明帝誅戮蕃戚，江州刺史桂陽王休範以人凡獲全。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had slaughtered the imperial kin; the Prince of Guiyang, Liu Xiufan, governor of Jiangzhou, alone survived entire because he was regarded as a mediocrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had cut down the imperial clansmen. Only Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang and governor of Jiangzhou, lived—spared because men thought him a nobody.

sentences.zh: 及蒼梧王立，更有窺窬之望，密與左右閹人於後堂習馳馬，招聚亡命。

translations.literal: When the Depraved Earl of Gusu was enthroned, Xiufan again harbored designs of usurpation, secretly practicing horsemanship in the rear hall with his eunuch intimates and gathering fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: When the Depraved Earl took the throne, Xiufan again nursed treason. In the rear hall he drilled horsemanship with his eunuchs in secret and gathered desperate men.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年五月，舉兵於尋陽，收略官民，數日便辦，眾二萬人，騎五百匹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second Yuanhui year he raised troops at Xunyang, levied officials and commoners, and in a few days was ready: twenty thousand men and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yuanhui year two he rose at Xunyang, swept up officials and commoners, and within days had twenty thousand men and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 發盆口，悉乘商旅船舫。

translations.literal: He set out from Penkou, all aboard merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed from Penkou on merchant craft alone.

sentences.zh: 大雷戍主杜道欣、鵲頭戍主劉諐期告變，朝廷惶駭。

translations.literal: The garrison commanders Du Daoxin at Dalei and Liu Yanqi at Quetou reported the rebellion; the court was struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Du Daoxin at Dalei and Liu Yanqi at Quetou sent word of the revolt, and the court panicked.

sentences.zh: 太祖與護軍褚淵、征北張永、領軍劉勔、僕射劉秉、游擊將軍戴明寶、驍騎將軍阮佃夫、右軍將軍王道隆、中書舍人孫千齡、員外郎楊運長集中書省計議，莫有言者。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng with Chu Yuan, Protector of the Army; Zhang Yong, North Campaign general; Liu Xu, Army Director; Liu Bing, Grand Master; Dai Mingbao, Strike-General; Ruan Dianfu, Valiant Cavalry general; Wang Daolong, General of the Right Army; Sun Qianling, Secretariat Aide; and Yang Yunchang, outside cadet, gathered at the Secretariat to deliberate—and none would speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng met at the Secretariat with Chu Yuan, Zhang Yong, Liu Xu, Liu Bing, Dai Mingbao, Ruan Dianfu, Wang Daolong, Sun Qianling, and Yang Yunchang to plan the response. No one spoke.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「昔上流謀逆，皆因淹緩，至於覆敗。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng said, "In the past rebellions on the upper Yangtze all failed through delay and slackness, ending in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng said, "Every upriver revolt in memory was lost to hesitation and slow movement.

sentences.zh: 休範必遠懲前失，輕兵急下，乘我無備。

translations.literal: Xiufan is sure to take distant warning from past failures and come down light and fast, catching us unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan will take those lessons to heart and strike light and fast while we are still unready.

sentences.zh: 今應變之術，不宜念遠，若偏師失律，則大沮眾心。

translations.literal: Today's adaptive art must not dwell on distant schemes; if a detached column misses its measure, the army's heart will be deeply shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Our answer cannot be a distant plan. One misstep by a flank force will break the army's nerve.

sentences.zh: 宜頓新亭、白下，堅守宮掖、東府、石頭以待。

translations.literal: We should halt at Xinting and Baixia, and hold the palace quarters, the Eastern Establishment, and Stone City to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Xinting and Baixia, and lock the palace, the Eastern Establishment, and Stone City until they come.

sentences.zh: 賊千里孤軍，後無委積，求戰不得，自然瓦解。

translations.literal: The rebels are a lone army a thousand li from home, with no stores behind them; unable to force a battle, they will collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They are a thousand li from home with empty magazines. Denied battle, they will fall apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 我請頓新亭以當其鋒；

translations.literal: I ask to halt at Xinting to meet their point;
translations.idiomatic: I will take Xinting and meet their van;

sentences.zh: 征北可以見甲守白下；

translations.literal: the North Campaign general can show armor and hold Baixia;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong can show his armor at Baixia;

sentences.zh: 中堂舊是置兵地，領軍宜屯宣陽門為諸軍節度；

translations.literal: the central hall was formerly the place for troops—the Army Director should encamp at Xuanyang Gate to coordinate all armies;
translations.idiomatic: the Army Director should hold Xuanyang Gate, where troops were always stationed, and direct the rest;

sentences.zh: 諸貴安坐殿中，右軍諸人不須競出，我自前驅，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: let the high ministers sit at ease in the hall; the men of the Right Army need not all rush out—I myself will lead the van, and the rebels are sure to be broken."
translations.idiomatic: the great ministers should stay seated in the hall; the Right Army need not crowd forward. I will ride in front myself, and the rebels will break."

sentences.zh: 」因索筆下議，竝注同。

translations.literal: He called for brush and wrote the plan for discussion; all noted their assent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for brush and paper, set the plan down, and every man signed his name to it.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人孫千齡與休範有密契，獨曰：「宜依舊遣軍據梁山、魯顯閒，右衞若不出白下，則應進頓南州。

translations.literal: Secretariat aide Sun Qianling had a secret compact with Xiufan and alone said, "We should follow precedent and send troops to hold the line between Liangshan and Luyan; if the Right Guard does not come out to Baixia, we should advance to encamp at Nanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qianling, who was in secret league with Xiufan, alone objected: "Send the army to the gap between Liangshan and Luyan as before. If the Right Guard will not leave Baixia, we should move up to Nanzhou."

sentences.zh: 」太祖正色曰：「賊今已近，梁山豈可得至。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng, with stern countenance, said, "The rebels are close now—how could we reach Liangshan?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng's face hardened. "The enemy is almost here. Liangshan is out of reach.

sentences.zh: 新亭既是兵衝，所以欲死報國耳。

translations.literal: Xinting is the military choke point—that is why I mean to stake my life for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xinting is where the road narrows. That is why I am willing to die there for the realm.

sentences.zh: 常日乃可屈曲相從，今不得也。

translations.literal: On ordinary days one might bend to follow others; today one may not."
translations.idiomatic: On other days I might yield. Not today."

sentences.zh: 」座起，太祖顧謂劉勔曰：「領軍已同鄙議，不可改易。

translations.literal: He rose from his seat and turned to Liu Xu: "The Army Director has already agreed with my humble view—it cannot be altered."
translations.idiomatic: He stood and said to Liu Xu, "The Army Director has already sided with me. There is no changing this."

sentences.zh: 」乃單車白服出新亭。

translations.literal: He then rode out alone in plain white to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to Xinting alone, in plain white dress.

sentences.zh: 加太祖使持節、都督征討諸軍、平南將軍，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng was further given credential staff as envoy, overall command of punitive forces, the rank General Who Pacifies the South, and one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He was made envoy with full staff, commander of all punitive forces, General Who Pacifies the South, and given a band of martial music.

sentences.zh: 治新亭城壘未畢，賊前軍已至，太祖方解衣高臥，以安眾心。

translations.literal: Before the Xinting ramparts were finished, the rebel vanguard had arrived. Xiao Daocheng had just stripped off his clothes and lain down high on the wall to steady the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel van reached Xinting before its walls were done. Xiao Daocheng stripped, stretched out on the rampart, and feigned ease to calm the ranks.

sentences.zh: 乃索白虎幡，登西垣，使寧朔將軍高道慶、羽林監陳顯達、員外郎王敬則浮舸與賊水戰，自新林至赤岸，大破之，燒其船艦，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: He then summoned the White Tiger banner, mounted the western wall, and had the Pacifying North general Gao Daoqing, the Feathered Forest inspector Chen Xianda, and the outside cadet Wang Jingze float boats to fight the rebels on the water from Xinlin to Chian, routing them utterly, burning their ships, with very many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the White Tiger banner, took the western wall, and sent Gao Daoqing, Chen Xianda, and Wang Jingze out on light craft. From Xinlin to Chian they shattered the rebel fleet, burned the ships, and left the water strewn with dead.

sentences.zh: 賊步上新林，太祖馳使報劉勔，急開大小桁，撥淮中船舫，悉渡北岸。

translations.literal: The rebel infantry ascended Xinlin. Xiao Daocheng sent a swift messenger to Liu Xu to open the great and small bridges at once, shift boats on the Huai, and ferry all to the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel foot came up through Xinlin. Xiao Daocheng galloped word to Liu Xu to open the great and small bridges, gather every boat on the Huai, and ferry the force to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 休範乘肩輿率眾至壘南，上遣寧朔將軍黃回、馬軍主周盤龍將步騎出壘對陣。

translations.literal: Xiufan in a sedan chair led his host to the south of the ramparts. The emperor sent the Pacifying North general Huang Hui and the cavalry commander Zhou Panlong with foot and horse out of the ramparts to form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan came in a litter at the head of his host to the foot of the wall. The throne sent Huang Hui and the cavalry chief Zhou Panlong with mixed foot and horse out to meet him in line.

sentences.zh: 休範分兵攻壘東，短兵接戰，自巳至午，眾皆失色。

translations.literal: Xiufan divided his force to attack the east of the ramparts; at close quarters they joined battle from the si hour to noon, and all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan split his men to storm the east face. Steel met at arm's length from mid-morning to noon, and every face went white.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「賊雖多而亂，尋破也。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng said, "The rebels are many but disorderly—they will soon be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng said, "They are numerous but in disarray. They will break in a moment."

sentences.zh: 」楊運長領三齊射手七百人，引彊命中，故賊不得逼城。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang led seven hundred Three-Qi archers; drawing to full draw they hit every mark, so the rebels could not press the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang led seven hundred archers of the Three Qi. Every shaft he loosed found its mark, and the rebels could not close on the wall.

sentences.zh: 未時，張敬兒斬休範首。

translations.literal: At the wei hour Zhang Jing'er cut off Xiufan's head.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-afternoon Zhang Jing'er took Xiufan's head.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣隊主陳靈寶送首還臺，靈寶路中遇賊軍，埋首道側。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng sent the squad commander Chen Lingbao to carry the head back to the capital; on the road Lingbao met rebel troops and buried the head beside the way.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng sent Chen Lingbao to bear the head to the capital. On the road Lingbao ran into rebels and buried the head by the wayside.

sentences.zh: 臺軍不見休範首，愈疑懼。

translations.literal: The capital army did not see Xiufan's head and grew all the more doubtful and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Without the head, the capital troops only grew more fearful and uncertain.

sentences.zh: 賊眾亦不知休範已死，別率杜黑蠡急攻壘東，司空主簿蕭惠朗數百人突入東門，叫噪至堂下，城上守門兵披退。

translations.literal: The rebel host also did not know Xiufan was already dead. A separate band under Du Heilai pressed the attack on the east of the ramparts; the Minister of Works chief clerk Xiao Huilang with several hundred men burst through the east gate, shouting all the way to the hall below; the gate guards on the wall gave way and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not know Xiufan was dead either. Du Heilai led a separate force in a rush on the east wall. Xiao Huilang, chief clerk to the Minister of Works, broke through the east gate with hundreds of men, yelling to the very hall. The gate guards on the wall broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 太祖挺身上馬，率數百人出戰，賊皆推楯而前，相去數丈，分兵橫射，太祖引滿將發，左右將戴仲緒舉楯扞之，箭應手飲羽，傷百餘人，賊死戰不能當，乃卻。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng straightened on horseback and led several hundred men out to fight. The rebels all pushed shields and advanced; when they were several zhang apart they split forces to shoot across. Xiao Daocheng drew to the full and was about to loose; the officer on his left Dai Zhongxu raised a shield to ward them off. Arrows buried their feathers in it at once. More than a hundred were wounded. The rebels fought to the death but could not stand before him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng mounted, drew his sword, and led several hundred men out. The enemy came on behind shields. At a few yards they split and shot from the flanks. He bent his bow to the ear; Dai Zhongxu on his left lifted a shield, and arrows sank to the feathers in the wood. More than a hundred fell. The rebels fought until they could not hold and drew back.

sentences.zh: 眾軍復得保城，與黑蠡拒戰，自晡達明旦，矢石不息。

translations.literal: The army again could hold the city and traded blows with Heilai from the hour of shen until dawn, arrows and stones without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison held again and fought Heilai from dusk until dawn without pause of bolt or stone.

sentences.zh: 其夜大雨，皷叫不復相聞，將士積日不得寢食，軍中馬夜驚，城內亂走，太祖秉燭正坐，厲聲呵止之，如此者數四。

translations.literal: That night a great rain fell; drums and cries could no longer be heard. The officers and soldiers had for days had neither sleep nor food. Horses in the army panicked in the night; inside the wall men ran in disorder. Xiao Daocheng held a candle and sat upright, shouting sternly to halt them—four times and more.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rain came down in torrents until drum and shout were drowned. For days the men had not slept or eaten. Horses stampeded in the dark; inside the wall men ran wild. Xiao Daocheng sat by candlelight and shouted them down, again and again, four times or more.

sentences.zh: 賊帥丁文豪設伏破臺軍於皁莢橋，直至朱雀桁，劉勔欲開桁，王道隆不從，勔及道隆竝戰沒。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Ding Wenhao laid an ambush and broke the capital army at Zaojia Bridge, reaching as far as Zhuque Bridge. Liu Xu wished to open the bridge; Wang Daolong would not consent. Liu and Wang both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Ding Wenhao ambushed the capital force at Zaojia Bridge and drove through to Zhuque Bridge. Liu Xu wanted the bridge opened; Wang Daolong refused. Both Liu and Wang fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 初，勔高尚其意，託造園宅，名為「東山」，頗忽世務。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu had elevated his mind, entrusting the building of gardens and mansions named "Eastern Hill," and largely neglected worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu had turned to high-minded ease, building a garden estate he called Eastern Hill, and let the world go by.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂之曰：「將軍以顧命之重，任兼內外，主上春秋未幾，諸王竝幼沖，上流聲議，遐邇所聞，此是將軍艱難之日，而將軍深尚從容，廢省羽翼，一朝事至，雖悔

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng said to him, "General, you bear the weight of a deathbed charge and duties within and without. The sovereign's years are few; all the princes are young and tender. The talk upriver is heard far and near. This is the general's hour of trial—yet the general deeply esteems ease, neglects his wings. When the matter comes in a morning, though one may regret
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng told him, "You carry a deathbed trust and command inside and outside the court. The emperor is a child; the princes are infants. Rumor on the upper river is heard everywhere. This is your hard season—yet you prize leisure and strip away your own wings. When crisis comes overnight, though you may regret

translations.literal: (it)
translations.idiomatic: —it—

sentences.zh: 〔何〕追。

translations.literal: [how] pursue.
translations.idiomatic: [how] can you make it right?

sentences.zh: 」勔竟不納。

translations.literal: Liu would not heed it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Liu never took the warning.

sentences.zh: 賊進至杜姥宅，車騎典籤茅恬開東府納賊，冠軍將軍沈懷明於石頭奔散，張永潰於白下，宮內傳新亭亦陷，太后執蒼梧王手泣曰：「天下敗矣！

translations.literal: The rebels advanced to the Du family estate outside the walls. The Establishment of the Chariots registry officer Mao Tian opened the Eastern Establishment to admit them. Champion General Shen Huaiming scattered his men at Stone City; Zhang Yong was routed at Baixia. Inside the palace came word that Xinting too had fallen. The empress dowager took the Depraved Earl by the hand and wept, saying, "The realm is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pushed to the Du family manor. Mao Tian of the Chariot Establishment opened the Eastern Palace to them. Shen Huaiming, Champion General, broke and fled from Stone City; Zhang Yong was beaten at Baixia. Word ran through the palace that Xinting had fallen. The empress dowager seized the Depraved Earl's hand and wept, "The empire is undone!"

sentences.zh: 」太祖遣軍主陳顯達、任農夫、張敬兒、周盤龍等，從石頭濟淮，閒道從承明門入衞宮闕。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng sent the army commanders Chen Xianda, Ren Nongfu, Zhang Jing'er, and Zhou Panlong and others to cross the Huai from Stone City by a bypath and enter through the Chenming Gate to guard the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng sent Chen Xianda, Ren Nongfu, Zhang Jing'er, Zhou Panlong, and others from Stone City across the Huai by a hidden route and in through Chenming Gate to hold the palace.

sentences.zh: 休範既死，典籤許公與詐稱休範在新亭，士庶惶惑，詣壘投名者千數，太祖隨得輒燒之，乃列兵登城北，謂曰：「劉休範父子先昨皆已即戮，屍在南岡下，身是蕭平南，諸君善見觀！

translations.literal: Though Xiufan was already dead, the registry officer Xu Gonghe falsely claimed Xiufan was still at Xinting; officials and commoners were terrified, and those who came to the ramparts to register their names numbered in the thousands. Xiao Daocheng burned each list as he received it, then drew up his ranks on the north wall and said, "Liu Xiufan and his son were executed yesterday; their corpses lie below the southern hill. I am Xiao the Pacifier of the South—look well upon me!
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan was dead, but Xu Gonghe of the registry spread word that he still held Xinting. Gentry and commoners panicked; thousands came to the wall to give their names. Xiao Daocheng burned every list on receipt, then lined the north wall and called out, "Liu Xiufan and his son were killed yesterday. Their bodies lie on the southern slope. I am Xiao the Pacifier of the South—see me for yourselves!

sentences.zh: 君等名皆已焚除，勿有懼也。

translations.literal: Your names have all been burned away—have no fear."
translations.idiomatic: Your names are already ash. You have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」臺分遣眾軍擊杜姥宅、宣陽門諸賊，皆破平之。

translations.literal: The capital dispatched the various armies to strike the rebels at the Du family estate and at Xuanyang Gate; all were broken and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent its columns against the Du manor and Xuanyang Gate; every band was crushed.

sentences.zh: 太祖振旅凱入，百姓緣道聚觀，曰：「全國家者此公也。」

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng led the army home in triumph; commoners lined the road to watch, saying, "This is the man who saved the state."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng marched in victory. The people crowded the roads and said, "The realm stands because of this man."

sentences.zh: 太祖與袁粲、褚淵、劉秉引咎解職，不許。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng with Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing offered to resign and accept blame; the court would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng, Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing asked to lay down office and take blame. The throne refused.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、中領軍、都督南兖徐兖青冀五州軍事、鎮軍將軍、南兖州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Palace Attendant, Central Army Director, Supervisor of all military affairs of the five provinces of South Yanzhou, Xuzhou, Yanzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, General Who Guards the Army, and Inspector of South Yanzhou, with credential staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant, Central Army Director, supervisor of the five provinces from South Yanzhou through Jizhou, General Who Guards the Army, and inspector of South Yanzhou, keeping his staff.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to duke and his fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke, with two thousand households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲分其功，請益粲等戶，更日入直決事，號為「四貴」。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng wished to share the merit and asked that Yuan Can and the others receive additional households; they entered court on alternate days to decide affairs and were called the "Four Exalted."
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to spread the credit, he asked that Yuan Can and the others receive added households too. They took turns in court to decide policy and were called the Four Exalted.

sentences.zh: 秦時有太后、穰侯、涇陽、高陵君，稱為「四貴」，至是乃復有焉。

translations.literal: In Qin times there had been the empress dowager, Marquis of Rang, Lord of Jingyang, and Lord of Gaoling, called the "Four Exalted"; now they existed again.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the empress dowager, the Marquis of Rang, and the lords of Jingyang and Gaoling had been called the Four Exalted; now the title lived again.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太祖尚書左僕射，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xiao Daocheng was further made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was also made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 休範平後，蒼梧王漸行凶暴，南徐州刺史建平王景素少有令譽，朝野歸心。

translations.literal: After Xiufan was pacified, the Depraved Earl grew daily more violent. The Prince of Pingping, Liu Jingsu, governor of South Xuzhou, had long enjoyed a fine reputation, and court and country looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiufan was down, the Depraved Earl turned ever more savage. Liu Jingsu, Prince of Pingping and governor of South Xuzhou, was young but widely trusted; men looked to him.

sentences.zh: 景素亦潛為自全之計，布款誠於太祖，太祖拒而不納。

translations.literal: Jingsu also secretly made plans for his own safety, offering his loyalty to Xiao Daocheng, who refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu too plotted to save himself and sent pledges of loyalty to Xiao Daocheng, who would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 七月，羽林監袁祗奔景素，便舉兵，太祖出屯玄武湖，遣眾軍北討，事平乃還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Feathered Forest inspector Yuan Zhi fled to Jingsu and at once raised troops. Xiao Daocheng went out to encamp at Xuanwu Lake, sent the armies north to punish him, and returned only when the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuan Zhi of the Feathered Forest defected to Jingsu and rose in arms. Xiao Daocheng camped at Xuanwu Lake, sent the hosts north, and came back only when the revolt was crushed.

sentences.zh: 太祖威名既重，蒼梧王深相猜忌，幾加大禍。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng's prestige was now weighty; the Depraved Earl deeply suspected him and nearly brought great calamity upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng's name weighed on every mind. The Depraved Earl hated and feared him and nearly had him killed.

sentences.zh: 陳太妃罵之曰：「蕭道成有功於國，今若害之，後誰復為汝著力者？

translations.literal: Consort Chen the Honored reviled him, saying, "Xiao Daocheng has served the state with merit—if you harm him now, who afterward will fight for you?"
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Chen cursed the emperor: "Xiao Daocheng has earned the realm. Kill him, and who will ever strike a blow for you again?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖密謀廢立。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng secretly plotted deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng began to plan the removal of the throne.

sentences.zh: 五年七月戊子，帝微行出北湖，常單馬先走，羽儀禁衞隨後追之，於堤塘相蹈藉，左右張互兒馬墜湖，帝怒，取馬置光明亭前，自馳騎刺殺之，因共屠割，與左右作羌胡伎為樂。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi in the seventh month of the fifth year the emperor slipped out to the northern lake. He always rode ahead alone; ceremonial guards and household troops chased after. On the embankment they trampled one another. The attendant Zhang Hu'er's horse fell into the lake. The emperor in rage took the horse to the Bright Light Pavilion forecourt, himself galloped and speared it to death, then together with his intimates butchered it and made Qiang and Hu entertainments for sport.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh month, day wuzi of year five, the emperor stole out to the northern lake. He always galloped ahead alone while guards and household troops pounded after. On the dike men tripped over one another. Zhang Hu'er's horse went into the water. The emperor, furious, had the animal brought to the Bright Light Pavilion, ran it down himself with a lance, then carved it up with his companions and staged Qiang and Hu horse games for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又於蠻岡賭跳。

translations.literal: He also gambled at leaping on the Barbarian Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He wagered on jumping games at the Barbarian Mound.

sentences.zh: 際夕乃還仁壽殿東阿氈屋中寢。

translations.literal: Only at dusk did he return to sleep in the felt tent east of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He did not return until evening, to sleep in the felt tent east of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.

sentences.zh: 語左右楊玉夫：「伺織女度，報我。

translations.literal: He told the attendant Yang Yufu, "Watch for the weaving girls to pass and report to me."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yang Yufu, "When the weaving girls go by, let me know."

sentences.zh: 」時殺害無常，人懷危懼。

translations.literal: At that time killings had no fixed pattern; men lived in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Murder had no pattern then; every man feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 玉夫與其黨陳奉伯等二十五人同謀，於氈屋中取千牛刀殺蒼梧王，稱敕，使廂下奏伎，因將首出與王敬則，敬則送太祖。

translations.literal: Yufu with his fellows Chen Fengbo and twenty-three others together plotted; in the felt tent they took the thousand-catty blade and killed the Depraved Earl, proclaiming an edict, and had the side chambers play music. They then carried the head out to Wang Jingze, and Jingze delivered it to Xiao Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yufu joined Chen Fengbo and twenty-three others in a plot. In the felt tent they took the great ox-knife and slew the Depraved Earl, cried an edict, and ordered musicians in the side hall to play. They bore the head to Wang Jingze, and Jingze brought it to Xiao Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖夜從承明門乘常所騎赤馬入，殿內驚怖，既知蒼梧王死，咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: That night Xiao Daocheng entered on the red horse he always rode through the Chenming Gate. The palace was struck with terror; when they knew the Depraved Earl was dead, all cried "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiao Daocheng rode his usual red horse in through Chenming Gate. The halls shook with fear; once they knew the Depraved Earl was dead, every voice shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 及太祖踐阼，號此馬為「龍驤將軍」，世謂為「龍驤赤」。

translations.literal: When Xiao Daocheng ascended the throne, this horse was titled "General Dragon Charger," and men called it "Red Dragon Charger."
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he gave the horse the title General Dragon Charger; folk called it the Red Dragon Charger.

sentences.zh: 明日，太祖戎服出殿庭槐樹下，召四貴集議。

translations.literal: The next day Xiao Daocheng in martial dress came out under the court-yard locust tree and summoned the Four Exalted to council.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he came out in armor under the locust in the court and called the Four Exalted to meet.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂劉秉曰：「丹陽國家重戚，今日之事，屬有所歸。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng said to Liu Bing, "Danyang is the realm's great imperial kinship. Today's affair must find its proper home."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Liu Bing, "Danyang is the throne's chief kinsman. What is done today must have its rightful heir."

sentences.zh: 」秉讓不當。

translations.literal: Bing declined as unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Bing refused, saying it was not his place.

sentences.zh: 太祖次讓袁粲，粲又不受。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng next yielded to Yuan Can, and Can also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng turned to Yuan Can next; Can would not take it either.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃下議，備法駕詣東城，迎立順帝。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng then set the matter before council, fully preparing the imperial equipage to go to the eastern palace and welcome the establishment of Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Then he put it to the assembly, ordered the full imperial train to the eastern palace, and had Emperor Shun brought to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是長刀遮粲、秉等，各失色而去。

translations.literal: Long knives then barred Yuan Can, Bing, and the others; each paled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Long knives closed around Yuan Can and Bing; each man went white and left.

sentences.zh: 甲午，太祖移鎮東府，與袁粲、褚淵、劉秉各甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu Xiao Daocheng moved his headquarters to the Eastern Establishment. He and Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing each entered the hall with fifty armed men.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiawu he shifted his seat to the Eastern Establishment. He and Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing entered the hall each with fifty armored guards.

sentences.zh: 丙申，進位侍中、司空、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍，持節、都督、刺史如故，封竟陵郡公，邑五千戶，給油幢絡車，班劍三十人。

translations.literal: On day bingshen he was advanced to Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Recorder of the Affairs of the Master of Writing, and General of Agile Cavalry, with credential staff, overall command, and inspectorates unchanged; enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling commandery with a fief of five thousand households; granted an oil-canopy carriage and thirty halberd bearers.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingshen he rose to Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Recorder of the Master of Writing, while keeping his staff, his overall command, and his provincial posts; he was made Duke of Jingling with five thousand households, given an oil-canopy carriage, and attended by thirty halberd bearers.

sentences.zh: 太祖固辭上台，即驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng firmly declined the highest offices and remained General of Agile Cavalry with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng refused the top posts and held to General of Agile Cavalry with a household matching the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，進督南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On day gengxu he was advanced to supervise South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu his authority was extended over South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 封楊玉夫等二十五人爵邑各有差。

translations.literal: Yang Yufu and twenty-four others were enfeoffed with ranks and fiefs in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufu and twenty-four others received noble ranks and fiefs, each according to merit.
