sentences.zh: 十月戊辰，又進督豫、司二州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, day wuchen, he was again advanced to supervise Yu and Si provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, day wuchen, he was given supervision of Yu and Si as well.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州刺史沈攸之與太祖於景和世同直殿省，申以歡好，以長女義興公主妻攸之第三子元和。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jing Province Inspector Shen Youzhi and Xiao Daocheng had served together in the Palace Directorate in the Jinghe era; they pledged warm friendship, and Youzhi married his eldest daughter, Princess Yixing, to Youzhi's third son Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Shen Youzhi of Jing Province and Xiao Daocheng had shared duty in the Palace Directorate under Emperor Qianfei and sworn close friendship; Youzhi gave his eldest daughter, Princess Yixing, to his third son Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 攸之為郢州，值明帝晚運，陰有異圖。

translations.literal: When Youzhi was at Ying Province, in the late years of Emperor Ming he already harbored designs of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: While Youzhi held Ying Province, in Emperor Ming's last years he was already turning traitor in his heart.

sentences.zh: 自郢州遷為荊州，聚斂兵力，將吏逃亡，輒討質隣伍。

translations.literal: Transferred from Ying to Jing Province, he amassed troops and wealth; when officers and clerks fled, he at once held their neighboring households liable.
translations.idiomatic: Moved from Ying to Jing, he stockpiled men and money; any officer who ran was answered by collective punishment on his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 養馬至二千餘匹，皆分賦戍邏將士，使耕田而食，廩財悉充倉儲。

translations.literal: He raised more than two thousand horses, assigning them to garrison soldiers on the borders to plow for their food, while all granary wealth went into storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He bred more than two thousand horses and set border garrisons to feed them by the plow, while every grain of the treasury went into his own stores.

sentences.zh: 荊州作部歲送數千人仗，攸之割留，簿上供討四山蠻。

translations.literal: Each year Jing's workshop department sent several thousand weapons; Youzhi kept them back, while the ledgers recorded them as supplies for campaigns against the Four Mountains barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial workshops sent up thousands of weapons each year; Youzhi skimmed them off and wrote in the books that they were for war on the mountain tribes.

sentences.zh: 裝治戰艦數百千艘，沈之靈溪裏，錢帛器械巨積，朝廷畏之。

translations.literal: He fitted out several hundred or thousand warships and sank them in Lingxi Lane; money, silk, and arms heaped up until the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He built hundreds of warships and moored them in Lingxi Lane; coin, silk, and steel piled until the throne itself grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 高道慶家在華容，假還過江陵，道慶素便馬，攸之與宴飲，於聽事前合馬槊，道慶槊中破攸之馬鞍，攸之怒，索刃槊，道慶馳馬而出。

translations.literal: Gao Daoqing's family was at Huarong; on leave he passed through Jiangling. Daoqing was skilled with the horse; Youzhi feasted with him and they matched with horse-lances before the hall. Daoqing's lance struck and broke Youzhi's saddle; Youzhi in anger called for a bladed lance, and Daoqing galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daoqing, whose people were at Huarong, came home on leave through Jiangling. A fine horseman, he drank with Youzhi, and before the hall they tilted with cavalry lances until Daoqing's blow shattered Youzhi's saddle. Youzhi roared for a bladed lance; Daoqing spurred away.

sentences.zh: 還都，說攸之反狀，請三千人襲之，朝議慮其事難濟，太祖又保持不許。

translations.literal: Back in the capital he reported Youzhi's rebellious conduct and asked for three thousand men to strike him; court deliberation feared the plan could not succeed, and Xiao Daocheng too held him back and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he laid out Youzhi's treason and begged three thousand men to take him. The court doubted the odds, and Xiao Daocheng, keeping his own counsel, would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 太祖既廢立，遣攸之子司徒左長史元琰賫蒼梧王諸虐害器物示之，攸之未得即起兵，乃上表稱慶，并與太祖書推功。

translations.literal: After Xiao Daocheng had deposed and enthroned, he sent Youzhi's son, the Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Yuan Yan, bearing the objects with which the Lord of Cangwu had been tortured and killed, to show him; Youzhi could not rise at once but submitted a memorial of congratulation and wrote Xiao Daocheng assigning him the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiao Daocheng had set the throne right, he sent Youzhi's son Yuan Yan, chief clerk on the left, with the very things used to torment the Lord of Cangwu to death. Youzhi still could not march, so he sent a memorial of felicitation and a letter pushing the glory onto Xiao Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 攸之有素書十數行，常韜在裲襠角，云是明帝與己約誓。

translations.literal: Youzhi had a private letter of a dozen lines that he always hid in the corner of his vest, saying it was Emperor Ming's sworn pact with him.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi kept a private note of a dozen lines sewn in his vest, claiming it was Emperor Ming's bond with him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂舉兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he at last raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he raised his banners.

sentences.zh: 其妾崔氏、許氏諫攸之曰：「官年已老，那不為百口計！

translations.literal: His concubines Lady Cui and Lady Xu admonished Youzhi, saying, "My lord, you are already old—will you not think of your hundred mouths?"
translations.idiomatic: His concubines Cui and Xu pleaded with him: "My lord, you are old—will you spare a thought for the hundred lives under your roof?"

sentences.zh: 」攸之指裲襠角示之，稱太后令召己下都。

translations.literal: Youzhi pointed to the corner of his vest to show them, saying the empress dowager had ordered him summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi tapped the hidden letter in his vest and said the empress dowager herself had called him downriver to the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師恐懼。

translations.literal: The capital was struck with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fear ran through the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，太祖入居朝堂，命諸將西討，平西將軍黃回為都督前驅。

translations.literal: On day yimao Xiao Daocheng entered and took his seat in the court hall, ordered the generals west to punish the rebel, and made Pacifying West General Huang Hui commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On day yimao Xiao Daocheng moved into the court hall, sent the armies west against the rebel, and set Pacifying West Huang Hui at the head of the van.

sentences.zh: 前湘州刺史王蘊，太后兄子，少有膽力，以父揩名宦不達，欲以將途自奮。

translations.literal: Former Xiang Province Inspector Wang Yun, the empress dowager's elder sister's son, from youth had nerve and force; because his father Kui had not risen far in office, he meant to make his name on the general's road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, once inspector of Xiang and nephew to the empress dowager, had been bold since boyhood. His father Kui had never won high rank, and Yun meant to force his way up with the sword.

sentences.zh: 每撫刀曰：「龍淵、太阿，汝知我者。

translations.literal: He would stroke his blade and say, "Dragon Spring and Grand Might—you know me."
translations.idiomatic: He would run a hand along his blades and murmur, "Dragon Spring, Grand Might—you know who I am."

sentences.zh: 」叔父景文誡之曰：「阿答，汝滅我門戶！

translations.literal: His uncle Jingwen warned him, "A-Da, you will destroy our house!"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Jingwen warned him, "A-Da, you will bring our line to ashes!"

sentences.zh: 」蘊曰：「答與童烏貴賤覺異。

translations.literal: Yun said, "A-Da and Tongwu are not the same in high or low."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "A-Da and Tongwu were never equals in birth or worth."

sentences.zh: 」童烏，景文子絢小字；

translations.literal: Tongwu was the childhood name of Jingwen's son Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Tongwu was the pet name of Jingwen's son Xuan;

sentences.zh: 答，蘊小字也。

translations.literal: A-Da was Yun's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: A-Da was Yun's own pet name.

sentences.zh: 蘊遭母喪罷任，還至巴陵，停舟一月，日與攸之密相交構。

translations.literal: Yun, mourning his mother, left office and returned as far as Baling, where he moored a month, meeting daily with Youzhi in secret conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died Yun left his post and sailed back to Baling, where he lay at anchor a full month, plotting each day with Youzhi in secret.

sentences.zh: 時攸之未便舉兵，蘊乃下達郢州。

translations.literal: Youzhi was not yet ready to rise; Yun therefore went down to Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was not ready to move; Yun went on to Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 世祖為郢州長史，蘊期世祖出弔，因作亂據郢城，世祖知之，不出。

translations.literal: The future Emperor Wu was chief clerk at Ying; Yun timed his condolence visit, meaning to seize the city in revolt when he came out; the future emperor knew it and would not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wu was chief clerk at Ying. Yun waited for him to come out for mourning so he could seize the city in revolt; the prince saw through it and stayed within.

sentences.zh: 蘊還至東府前，又期太祖出，太祖又不出弔，再計不行，外謀愈固。

translations.literal: Yun returned before the Eastern Establishment and again timed Xiao Daocheng's coming out; Xiao Daocheng again would not go to mourn; when the second plot failed, the outer conspiracy only grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yun came back to wait before the Eastern Establishment and again timed Xiao Daocheng's exit; again Xiao Daocheng would not attend the mourning. With two schemes spoiled, the open plot only hardened.

sentences.zh: 司徒袁粲、尚書令劉秉見太祖威權稍盛，慮不自安，與蘊及黃回等相結舉事，殿內宿衞主帥，無不協同。

translations.literal: Secretary Yuan Can and Director of the Master of Writing Liu Bing, seeing Xiao Daocheng's power wax daily, feared they could not keep their place; with Yun and Huang Hui and others they joined in action, and among the palace night guards and commanders there was none who did not go along.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can of the Secretariat and Liu Bing, director of the Master of Writing, watched Xiao Daocheng's power swell and feared for their seats. With Yun, Huang Hui, and the rest they set a rising afoot, and among the night guards of the inner palace not one stood aside.

sentences.zh: 攸之反問初至，太祖往石頭與粲謀議，粲稱疾不相見。

translations.literal: When word first came that Youzhi had rebelled, Xiao Daocheng went to Stone City to consult with Can; Can pleaded illness and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: At the first news of Youzhi's revolt Xiao Daocheng went to Stone City to take counsel with Can; Can claimed sickness and shut the door.

sentences.zh: 剋壬申夜起兵據石頭，劉秉恇怯，晡時，從丹陽郡載婦女入石頭，朝廷不知也。

translations.literal: They fixed the night of day renshen to rise and hold Stone City. Liu Bing was timid; in the afternoon he had women of Danyang commandery carried into Stone City by boat, and the court knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They set the night of renshen to seize Stone City. Liu Bing was faint of heart; in the afternoon he had women ferried in from Danyang commandery, and the court suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 其夜，丹陽丞王遜告變，秉從弟領軍

translations.literal: That night Danyang Assistant Wang Xun reported the plot; Bing's younger cousin, Defender of the Palace
translations.idiomatic: That night Danyang's assistant Wang Xun raised the alarm; Bing's younger cousin, defender of the palace

translations.literal: (Tao)
translations.idiomatic: —Tao—

sentences.zh: 〔韞〕及直閤將軍卜伯興等嚴兵為內應。

translations.literal: [Yun] and Chief of the Direct Office Bu Boxing and others readied troops as inner accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Chief of the Direct Office Bu Boxing, and the rest armed men within as their inner hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖命王敬則於宮內誅之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng ordered Wang Jingze to execute them inside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng sent Wang Jingze to cut them down inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將攻石頭，王蘊將數百精手帶甲赴粲，城門已閉，官軍又至，乃散。

translations.literal: He dispatched the generals to attack Stone City. Wang Yun led several hundred picked men in armor to join Can, but the gate was already shut, the government troops had arrived, and they scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals against Stone City. Wang Yun rushed with several hundred armored picked men to Can's side, but the gates were shut, the loyal troops were already there, and Yun's band broke apart.

sentences.zh: 眾軍攻石頭，斬粲，劉秉走雒檐湖，蘊逃鬪場，並禽斬之。

translations.literal: The massed armies stormed Stone City, beheaded Can, Liu Bing fled to Luoyan Lake, Yun fled to the execution ground, and both were captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The columns took Stone City and struck off Can's head. Liu Bing ran for Luoyan Lake, Yun for the execution ground; both were taken and slain.

sentences.zh: 粲位任雖重，無經世之略，踈放好酒，步屧白楊郊野閒，道遇一士大夫，便呼與酣飲。

translations.literal: Though Can's office was weighty, he had no strategy for ordering the age; he was loose and fond of wine, walking in sandals through the white poplar wilds beyond the suburbs, and if he met a gentleman on the road he would call him to drink deep.
translations.idiomatic: Can's rank was great but he had no gift for governing the times. He was careless and in love with wine, strolling in sandals through the white poplars outside the walls, and any scholar he met on the road he would drag into his cup.

sentences.zh: 明日，此人謂被知顧，到門求通，粲曰：「昨飲酒無偶，聊相要耳。

translations.literal: Next day the man, thinking himself singled out for favor, came to the gate asking audience; Can said, "Yesterday I drank without a match and only invited you for company."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the man, sure he had been noticed, came to the gate for an audience. Can said, "Yesterday I lacked a drinking partner and only asked you along."

sentences.zh: 」竟不與相見。

translations.literal: In the end he would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: He never received him.

sentences.zh: 嘗作五言詩云：「訪迹雖中宇，循寄乃滄州。

translations.literal: He once composed a pentasyllabic poem saying, "I trace footsteps though within the realm, yet my heart lodges on the dark sea."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a five-word poem: "I walk the middle kingdom, yet my heart is moored on the dark sea."

sentences.zh: 」蓋其志也。

translations.literal: That was his mind.
translations.idiomatic: That was the man he meant to be.

sentences.zh: 劉秉少以宗室清謹見知，孝武世，秉弟遐坐通嫡母殷氏養女，殷亡口中血出，眾疑行毒害，孝武使秉從弟祗諷秉啟證其事。

translations.literal: Liu Bing from youth was known among the imperial clan for purity and caution. In Emperor Xiaowu's time Bing's younger brother Xia was accused of relations with his stepmother Lady Yin's foster daughter; when Yin died blood came from her mouth, and the crowd suspected poison. Xiaowu had Bing's cousin Zhi urge Bing to memorialize and prove the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing had been known since youth in the clan for sober care. Under Emperor Xiaowu his brother Xia was accused of lying with their stepmother Lady Yin's foster daughter; when Yin died with blood on her lips many cried poison. The emperor sent Bing's cousin Zhi to press him to testify.

sentences.zh: 秉曰：「行路之人，尚不應爾，今日迺可一門同盡，無容奉敕。

translations.literal: Bing said, "Even a man on the road should not be treated so; today you would have one house perish together—I cannot obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "A stranger on the road would deserve better than this; now you would wipe out a whole house at once. I will not carry out the order."

sentences.zh: 」眾以此稱之。

translations.literal: The crowd for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Men praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 故為明帝所任。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Ming trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: That was why Emperor Ming relied on him.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧廢，秉出集議，於路逢弟韞，韞開車迎問秉曰：「今日之事，固當歸兄邪？

translations.literal: When the Lord of Cangwu was deposed, Bing went out to the assembly for deliberation; on the road he met his brother Yun; Yun opened his carriage and greeted him, asking, "Today's affair—surely it should fall to you, elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Cangwu was cast down, Bing went to council. On the road he met Yun, who leaned from his carriage and asked, "Brother—surely today's prize is yours?"

sentences.zh: 」秉曰：「吾等已讓領軍矣。

translations.literal: Bing said, "We have already yielded to the Defender of the Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "We have already given way to the Defender of the Palace."

sentences.zh: 」韞槌胷曰：「君肉中詎有血！」

translations.literal: Yun beat his breast and said, "Is there blood in your flesh at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun struck his chest and cried, "Is there any blood in you at all!"

sentences.zh: 粲典籤莫嗣祖知粲謀，太祖召問嗣祖：「袁謀反，何不啟聞？

translations.literal: Can's registrar Mo Sizu knew Can's plot; Xiao Daocheng summoned and questioned Sizu: "Yuan plotted rebellion—why did you not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: Can's registrar Mo Sizu had known the plot. Xiao Daocheng called him in: "Yuan rebelled—why did you not speak?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣祖曰：「事主義無二心，雖死不敢泄也。

translations.literal: Sizu said, "Serving one's lord, righteousness admits no second heart; though I die I dare not betray him."
translations.idiomatic: Sizu said, "To serve a lord is to have one loyalty; I would die before I betrayed him."

sentences.zh: 」蘊嬖人張承伯藏匿蘊。

translations.literal: Yun's favorite Zhang Chengbai hid Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's favorite Zhang Chengbai concealed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖竝赦而用之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng pardoned both and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng pardoned them both and kept them in service.

sentences.zh: 黃回頓新亭，聞石頭鼓噪，率兵來赴之，朱雀𦨵有戍軍，受節度，不聽夜過，會石頭已平，因稱救援。

translations.literal: Huang Hui was encamped at Xinting; hearing the clamor at Stone City, he led troops to hurry there. At Zhuque Ford there was a garrison under command and it would not let him pass by night; when Stone City was already pacified he therefore claimed he had come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui lay at Xinting. Hearing uproar at Stone City he marched to join it, but the garrison at Zhuque Ford, under orders, barred him at night. When Stone City had already fallen he said he had come to save it.

sentences.zh: 太祖知而不言，撫之愈厚，遣回西上，流涕告別。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng knew yet said nothing, treated him all the more generously, sent him west again, and parted from him in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng knew and said nothing, only treated him the more kindly, sent him west again, and wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 太祖屯閱武堂，馳結軍旅。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng encamped at the Review of Arms Hall and swiftly rallied the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng took the Review of Arms Hall and whipped the host into order.

sentences.zh: 閏月辛丑，詔假黃鉞，率大眾出屯新亭中興堂，治嚴築壘。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, day xinchou, an edict lent him the yellow battle-axe; he led the great host out to encamp at the Hall of Middle Revival at Xinting, arrayed in order and threw up ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, day xinchou, he was lent the yellow battle-axe and led the main force to camp at the Hall of Middle Revival in Xinting, drawing up ranks and digging earthworks.

sentences.zh: 教曰：「河南稱慈，諒由掩胔，廣漢流仁，實存殯朽。

translations.literal: An instruction said: "Henan was called merciful because it covered the unburied dead; Guanghan was famed for benevolence because it preserved the rotting corpse."
translations.idiomatic: An instruction ran: "Henan won the name of mercy for covering the unburied; Guanghan won the name of kindness for tending the bones of the dead."

sentences.zh: 近袤製茲營，崇溝浚塹，古墟曩隧，時有湮移，深松茂草，或致刊薙。

translations.literal: Recently this camp was laid out broadly, its ditches deepened and moats cut; old ruins and former tunnels are sometimes lost, and deep pines and thick grass are sometimes cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Of late this camp has been widened, its trenches cut deep; old tombs and buried ways shift with time, and tall pines and heavy grass are sometimes cleared away.

sentences.zh: 憑軒動懷，巡隍增愴。

translations.literal: Leaning on the rail I am moved in heart; patrolling the rampart my grief grows.
translations.idiomatic: At the parapet the heart is stirred; along the wall grief deepens.

sentences.zh: 宜竝為收改葬，并設薄祀。」

translations.literal: Let all be gathered for reburial, and let lean sacrifices be set up as well."
translations.idiomatic: Let the dead be gathered and buried anew, and let simple rites be offered as well."

sentences.zh: 二年正月，沈攸之攻郢城不剋，眾潰，自經死，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Shen Youzhi attacked Ying city without taking it; his host broke; he hanged himself, and his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's first month Youzhi besieged Ying and failed. His army dissolved; he hanged himself, and his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙子，太祖旋鎮東府。

translations.literal: On day bingzi Xiao Daocheng returned to headquarters at the Eastern Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingzi Xiao Daocheng went back to his seat at the Eastern Establishment.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，進太祖太尉，增封三千戶，都督南徐、南兖、徐、兖、青、冀、司、豫、荊、雍、湘、郢、梁、益、廣、越十六州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On day guiwei in the second month he was advanced to Grand Marshal, with three thousand households added to his fief, and made commander of all military affairs in sixteen provinces: South Xu, South Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, Si, Yu, Jing, Yong, Xiang, Ying, Liang, Yi, Guang, and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On day guiwei in the second month he was made Grand Marshal, given three thousand more households, and set over sixteen provinces from South Xu to Yue.

sentences.zh: 太祖解驃騎，辭都督，不許，乃表送黃鉞。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng resigned the Agile Cavalry post and declined overall command; it was not permitted, and he therefore memorialized returning the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: He laid down Agile Cavalry and refused overall command; the throne would not hear it, so he sent back the yellow battle-axe in memorial.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，增班劍為四十人、甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: On day jiyou in the third month the halberd escort was increased to forty men and a hundred armored guards were allowed in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiyou in the third month his halberd escort rose to forty and a hundred armored men could enter the hall with him.

sentences.zh: 丙子，加羽葆鼓吹，餘竝如故。

translations.literal: On day bingzi he was given feathered canopy and drum escort; the rest was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingzi he received feathered canopy and drum escort; all else stood as before.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太祖誅鎮北將軍黃回。

translations.literal: On day xinmao Xiao Daocheng executed Pacifying North General Huang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinmao Xiao Daocheng put Pacifying North Huang Hui to death.

sentences.zh: 大明泰始以來，相承奢侈，百姓成俗。

translations.literal: From the Taishi and Taiyuan years of Daming onward, extravagance had passed from hand to hand until the people took it as custom.
translations.idiomatic: Since Daming's Taishi and Taiyuan reigns, luxury had been handed down until the folk wore it as habit.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，罷御府，省二尚方諸飾玩。

translations.literal: When Xiao Daocheng took the government he abolished the imperial workshops and cut the two Palace Workshops' ornaments and playthings.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Daocheng held the reins he shut the imperial workshops and stripped the two Palace Workshops of their gewgaws.

sentences.zh: 至是又上表禁民閒華偽雜物：不得以金銀為箔，馬乘具不得金銀度，不得織成繡裙，道路不得著錦履，不得用紅色為幡蓋衣服，不得翦綵帛為雜花，不得以綾作雜服飾，不得作鹿行錦及局腳檉柏床、牙箱籠雜物、綵帛作屏鄣、錦緣薦席，不得私作器仗，不得以七寶飾樂器又諸雜漆物，不得以金銀為花獸，不得輒鑄金銅為像。

translations.literal: At this time he again memorialized forbidding among the people flashy false goods: gold and silver must not be used as foil; horse trappings must not be gilt; woven brocade skirts are forbidden; on the road brocade shoes may not be worn; red may not be used for banners, covers, or clothing; colored silk must not be cut into ornamental flowers; damask may not be made into mixed ornaments; deer-pattern brocade, corner-legged camphor beds, ivory boxes and cages, silk screens, brocade-edged mats, private manufacture of arms, the seven treasures must not adorn musical instruments and miscellaneous lacquerware, gold and silver must not be made into floral beasts, and gold or copper must not be cast into images.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to curb vulgar luxury among the people: no gold or silver foil, no gilt harness, no brocade skirts, no silk shoes on the road, no red for banners or dress, no cut-silk flowers, no damask finery, no deer-brocade or camphor beds with splayed feet, no ivory cases or cages, no silk screens or brocade-edged mats, no private arms, no seven-jewel instruments or fancy lacquer, no gold or silver beasts, no casting of images in gold or copper.

sentences.zh: 皆須墨敕，凡十七條。

translations.literal: All require imperial ink; seventeen articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: Every item required the emperor's written order; there were seventeen clauses.

sentences.zh: 其中宮及諸王服用，雖依舊例，亦請詳衷。

translations.literal: As for the inner palace and the princes' use, though the old examples stand, he also asked that they be weighed with care.
translations.idiomatic: Even for the palace and the imperial princes, though old usage might stand, he asked that each case be judged with care.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，進位假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、太傅、領揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: On day bingwu in the ninth month he was advanced to Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, commander of all armies within and without, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Yang Province, with sword in the hall and shoes on the floor, no hurrying in court, and no name spoken when praised.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingwu in the ninth month he received the acting yellow battle-axe, command inside and outside the realm, the Grand Tutorship, and the governorship of Yangzhou, with sword in court and shoes on the dais, no need to hurry, and no name called in praise.

sentences.zh: 置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，使持節、太尉、驃騎大將軍、錄尚書、南徐州刺史如故。

translations.literal: Left and right chief clerks, marshals, attendants, aides, and subordinates were set at four each; he remained as Bearer of the Staff, Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Recorder of the Master of Writing, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four chief clerks, marshals, attendants, aides, and clerks were appointed to left and right; he kept his staff, grand marshal's seal, Agile Cavalry, the recorder's brush, and South Xu.

sentences.zh: 固辭，詔遣敦勸，乃受黃鉞，辭殊禮。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; an edict sent messengers to press him earnestly, and only then did he accept the yellow battle-axe and decline the special honors.
translations.idiomatic: He refused; the throne sent envoys to press him until he took the yellow battle-axe and turned away the extraordinary rites.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，給三望車。

translations.literal: On day jiayin he was given the three-peaked carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiayin he was granted the three-peaked carriage.

sentences.zh: 三年正月乙巳，太祖表蠲百姓逋負。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, day yisi, Xiao Daocheng memorialized remitting the people's overdue taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's first month, day yisi, he memorialized to cancel the people's tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，加前部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: On day bingchen the front feathered canopy and drum escort was added.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingchen he was given the front feathered canopy and drum escort.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，命太傅府依舊辟召。

translations.literal: On day dingsi the Grand Tutor's office was ordered to recruit as of old.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingsi the Grand Tutor's office was told to recruit officers as before.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，給太祖甲仗五百人，出入殿省。

translations.literal: On day dingmao five hundred armored men were given Xiao Daocheng for entering and leaving the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingmao he was given five hundred armored guards for the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 甲午，重申前命，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: On day jiawu the earlier orders were reaffirmed: sword in the hall, shoes on the floor, no hurrying in court, no name spoken when praised.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiawu the earlier grants were renewed: sword in court, shoes on the dais, no hurrying, no name in praise.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，詔進位相國，總百揆，封十郡為齊公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱遠遊冠，位在諸侯王上，加相國綠綟綬，其驃騎大將軍、揚州牧、南徐州刺史如故。

translations.literal: On day jiachen in the third month an edict advanced him to Chancellor of State, with charge of the hundred offices, enfeoffing ten commanderies as Duke of Qi with the full Nine Bestowals, adding the far-wandering cap with seal cord, rank above all princes, the green ribbon of the chancellor of state, while General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yangzhou, and Inspector of South Xuzhou remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiachen in the third month he was made Chancellor of State over the hundred offices, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi across ten commanderies with the Nine Bestowals, given the far-wandering cap and seal cord and rank above every prince, the chancellor's green ribbon, while Agile Cavalry, Yangzhou, and South Xu stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 太祖三讓，公卿敦勸固請，乃受。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng declined three times; the nobles and ministers pressed him earnestly until he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng refused three times; the court pressed until he yielded.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，策相國齊公曰：

translations.literal: On day jiayin the Duke of Qi, Chancellor of State, was enfeoffed by edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On day jiayin the edict enfeoffing the Duke of Qi, Chancellor of State, ran:

sentences.zh: :天地變通，莫大乎炎涼，懸象著明，莫崇乎日月。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth shift—nothing greater than heat and cold; the hung emblems show brightness—nothing loftier than sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth turn; nothing surpasses cold and heat. The signs above shine; nothing outranks sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 嚴冬播氣，貞松之操自高，光景時昏，若華之暎彌顯。

translations.literal: In deep winter breath spreads abroad and the pine's constancy rises high; when light and shadow darken, the flower's gleam only shines the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter breathes out and the pine stands higher; when the hour grows dim, the blossom's fire burns brighter.

sentences.zh: 是故英睿當亂而不移，忠賢臨危而盡節。

translations.literal: Therefore the heroic and wise, facing disorder, do not shift; the loyal and worthy, meeting peril, exhaust their duty.
translations.idiomatic: So the wise hold firm in chaos, and the loyal spend themselves at the brink.

sentences.zh: 自景和昏虐，王綱弛紊，太宗受命，紹開中興，運屬屯難，四郊多壘。

translations.literal: From the Jinghe reign's cruel madness the royal cords slackened and tangled; the Founding Emperor received the mandate and reopened the middle revival; the age met hardship piled upon hardship, and on four sides the ramparts multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jinghe's tyranny the bonds of rule had frayed; the Founding Emperor took the mandate and opened the middle revival; fortune met hardship after hardship, and on every quarter of the land a camp went up.

sentences.zh: 蕭將軍震威華戎，寔資義烈，康國濟民，於是乎在。

translations.literal: General Xiao shook awe through Hua and the barbarian borderlands, truly relying on righteous fierceness; to settle the state and succor the people—there he stood.
translations.idiomatic: General Xiao struck fear through the heartland and the frontier, leaning on righteous fire; to steady the realm and feed the people—that was his place.

sentences.zh: 朕以不造，夙罹閔凶。

translations.literal: I, lacking worth, from youth met with bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: I, unworthy, have known grief since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 嗣君失德，書契未紀。

translations.literal: The heir lost the Way, and the written covenant was not kept.
translations.idiomatic: The heir lost the Way, and the covenant of rule went unwritten.

sentences.zh: 威侮五行，虔劉九縣，神歇靈繹，海水羣飛，彝器已塵，宗禋誰主，綴旒之殆，未足為譬，豈直小宛興刺，黍離作歌而已哉。

translations.literal: He insulted the Five Agents and slaughtered the nine provinces; the spirits fell silent and omens failed; the sea waters rose in flight; the sacred vessels were already dust; who would lead the ancestral rites? The peril of the hanging beads is too slight a likeness—how could it be only the "Little Millet" raising its reproach or the "Millet Sigh" made into song?
translations.idiomatic: He outraged the Five Phases and ravaged the nine provinces; spirits slept and omens broke; the sea itself seemed to boil; the sacred vessels were dust; who would tend the altars? The danger to the crown is more than a dangling string can picture—not merely the sting of "Little Millet" or the lament of "Millet Sigh."

sentences.zh: 天贊皇宋，實啟明宰，爰登寡昧，纂承大業，鴻緒再維，閎基重造，高勳至德，振古絕倫。

translations.literal: Heaven aided Great Song and truly opened a bright minister; I, ascending in my dullness, inherited the great enterprise; the great thread was knit again, the broad foundation rebuilt; supreme merit and utmost virtue shake the ages and stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blessed Great Song and raised a luminous minister; I, dull as I am, took up the great work; the main thread was woven again, the wide base set anew; merit and virtue such as these have no peer in any age.

sentences.zh: 昔保衡翼殷，博陸匡漢，方斯蔑如也。

translations.literal: Of old Yi Yin winged Yin and Huo Guang righted Han—set beside this, they are as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin once steadied Yin, Huo Guang once righted Han—beside this they dwindle to nothing.

sentences.zh: 今將授公典禮，其敬聽朕命。

translations.literal: Now I shall confer on you the canonical rites; respectfully hear my command.
translations.idiomatic: Now I invest you with the canonical rites; hear my command with respect.

sentences.zh: :乃者，袁

translations.literal: : As of late, Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Of late, Yuan

translations.literal: (Liu)
translations.idiomatic: —Liu—

sentences.zh: 〔鄧〕構禍，寔繁有徒，子房不臣，稱兵協亂，跨蹈五湖，憑陵吳、越，浮祲虧辰，沈氛晦景，桴鼓振於王畿，鋒鏑交乎天邑。

translations.literal: [Deng] stirred calamity, and indeed a great host followed; Zifang was disloyal, raised arms in concerted rebellion, trampled the Five Lakes, and overran Wu and Yue; floating bale-clouds dimmed the constellations, sinking vapors darkened the sun, war-drums shook the royal domain, and blades crossed at the celestial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan raised rebellion with a multitude at his back; Liu Zifang turned traitor and joined arms in revolt, spanning the Five Lakes and pressing Wu and Yue; ill omens veiled the stars, murk swallowed the daylight, war-drums thundered at the capital gates, and steel clashed under the walls of the throne.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宮掖，將成茂草，言念邦國，翦為仇讎。

translations.literal: Looking back at the palace quarters, they were about to become rank grass; thinking on the realm, it was cut into sworn foes.
translations.idiomatic: The palace seemed ready to go to weeds; the kingdom itself was being carved into enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，人無固志。

translations.literal: At that time, no man held a firm will.
translations.idiomatic: In that hour, hearts failed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 公投袂殉難，超然奮發，執金板而先馳，登寅車而戒路，軍政端嚴，卒乘輯睦，麾鉞一臨，凶黨冰泮。

translations.literal: The Duke flung his sleeve to die for the crisis, rose transcendent in ardor, seized the golden tally-board and raced ahead, mounted the dawn-chariot and set out on the road; military rule was strict, chariots and riders kept order, and at one wave of his axe the villainous faction melted like ice.
translations.idiomatic: You tore free your sleeve to meet the peril, surged forward in a blaze of resolve, took the golden tally and rode at the van, boarded the dawn-chariot and took the road; discipline held the host, chariot and foot kept step, and at a single sweep of your command-staff the rebels dissolved like ice in spring.

sentences.zh: 此則霸業之基，勤王之始也。

translations.literal: This was the foundation of hegemony, the beginning of succoring the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That was the ground of empire, the first stroke of loyalty to the crown.

sentences.zh: 安都背叛，竊據徐方，敢率犬羊，陵虐淮滸，索兒愚悖，同惡相濟，天祚無象，背順歸逆，北鄙黔黎，奄墜塗炭，均人廢職，邊師告警。

translations.literal: Andu betrayed and seized Xu territory by stealth, daring to lead dog-and-goat hordes to abuse the Huai shore; Suo'er was foolish and perverse, aiding the same evil; Heaven's blessing showed no sign, and he turned from obedience to rebellion; the black-haired folk of the northern marches suddenly fell into charcoal; frontier officers abandoned their posts, and border armies sounded the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu rebelled and clutched the Xu region, driving barbarian rabble to ravage the Huai; Cheng So'er, witless and wild, joined the same crime; Heaven gave no omen of favor as men turned traitor; the people of the north were plunged into ash; garrisons threw down their duty, and the frontier flared with warning.

sentences.zh: 公受命宗祊，精貫朝日，擁節和門，氣踰霄漢，破釜之捷，斬馘蔽野，石梁之戰，禽其渠帥，保境全民，江陽即序。

translations.literal: The Duke received mandate at the ancestral temple, his spirit piercing the morning sun; he embraced the staff at the Harmonious Gate, his breath surpassing the Milky Way; at the victory of Broken Cauldron, slain heads covered the wilds; at the battle of Stone Bridge, he captured their chieftain; he preserved the borders and secured the people, and Jiangyang was brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: You took heaven's charge at the royal shrine, spirit bright as the rising sun; you bore the credential-staff at the Harmonious Gate, valor towering to the sky; at Broken Cauldron the slain heaped the fields; at Stone Bridge you took the rebel chief; you held the line and saved the people, and Jiangyang returned to peace.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 張淹迷昧，弗顧本朝，

translations.literal: Zhang Yan was deluded and dim, heedless of the court,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan lost his way and turned his back on the throne,

translations.literal: (Shou)
translations.idiomatic: —Shou—

sentences.zh: 〔爰〕自南區，志圖東夏，潛軍閒入，竊覬不虞。

translations.literal: [Hence] from the southern quarter he plotted the eastern realm, sent troops in secret, and coveted surprise.
translations.idiomatic: From the south he schemed against the eastern lands, stole in with hidden columns, and hunted for an unguarded hour.

sentences.zh: 于時江服未夷，皇塗荐阻。

translations.literal: At that time the Yangzi lands were not yet pacified, and the royal road was repeatedly blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The river country was still unsettled, and the throne's path lay choked again and again.

sentences.zh: 公忠誠慷慨，在險彌亮，深識九變，妙察五色，以寡制眾，所向風偃。

translations.literal: The Duke was loyal and generous, brighter in peril; he deeply knew the nine changes and subtly discerned the five colors; with the few he controlled the many, and wherever he turned, foes bowed like wind-bent grass.
translations.idiomatic: You met danger with fiercer loyalty, read the nine shifts of war, weighed every sign in the field, and with slender forces broke the mass; where you advanced, enemies fell like grass before the gale.

sentences.zh: 朝廷無東顧之憂，閩、越有來蘇之慶。

translations.literal: The court had no worry of looking east; Min and Yue won the joy of returning life.
translations.idiomatic: The throne need no longer fear the east; Fujian and Yue tasted deliverance at last.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 匈奴野心，侵掠疆埸，前師失律，王旅崩撓，灑血成川，伏尸千里。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu bore a wolf heart and raided the borders; the former army lost discipline, the royal host wavered and broke; blood was shed till it formed rivers, and the slain lay for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Northern hordes hungered for the marches; our front lines broke, the imperial columns crumbled; blood ran in streams, and the dead carpeted the roads for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 醜羯侜張，勢振彭、泗，乘勝長驅，窺覦京甸，冠帶之軌將湮，被髮之容行及。

translations.literal: The ugly Jie swelled insolent, their power shaking Peng and Si; pressing the victory in long pursuit, they eyed the capital district; the realm of caps and sashes was about to perish, and shaggy-haired foes were nearly upon us.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian hosts flaunted their strength from Pengcheng to the Si, drove hard toward the heartland, and fixed their gaze on the capital; the civilized world teetered on the brink, and wild men of the steppe were almost at the gate.

sentences.zh: 公奉辭伐罪，戒旦晨征，兵車始交，氛祲時蕩，弔死撫傷，弘宣皇澤，俾我淮、肥，復沾盛化。

translations.literal: The Duke bore the mandate to punish crime, warned the ranks at dawn and marched at morning; as soon as chariots met, baleful vapors were swept away; he mourned the dead and comforted the wounded, broadly proclaimed the imperial grace, and made our Huai and Fei bathe again in flourishing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: You took the throne's word to chastise evil, roused the army at daybreak and marched; the moment battle joined, the evil air cleared; you buried the fallen and healed the hurt, spread the emperor's mercy abroad, and brought Huai and Fei back under civil rule.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，獫狁孔熾，封豕長蛇，重窺上國。

translations.literal: From that time onward the Xianyun grew fiercely hot; the great boar and long serpent again peered at the upper realm.
translations.idiomatic: After that the northern foe burned hotter still; like a boar and serpent they turned their eyes once more upon the empire.

sentences.zh: 而世故相仍，師出日老，戰士無臨陣之心，戎卒有懷歸之思。

translations.literal: Yet age after age the same troubles returned; armies went forth and grew old in the field; warriors had no heart to face the line, and border soldiers longed for home.
translations.idiomatic: War followed war; campaigns dragged on until the troops were spent; men would not stand to fight, and the garrisons dreamed only of return.

sentences.zh: 是以下邳精甲，望風振恐，角城高壘，指日淪陷。

translations.literal: Therefore the elite armor of Xiapi trembled at the wind; the high walls of Jiaocheng were doomed within days.
translations.idiomatic: The hardened men of Xiapi quailed at rumor; the towers of Jiaocheng were marked to fall overnight.

sentences.zh: 公眷言王事，發憤忘食，躬擐甲冑，視險若夷，短兵纔接，巨猾鳥散，分疆畫界，開創青、兖。

translations.literal: The Duke, mindful of the king's business, burned with wrath and forgot to eat; he himself donned armor, treated peril as level ground; at close blades the great villains scattered like birds; he divided borders and drew boundaries, opening Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: You brooded on the throne's need, raged till you skipped meals, buckled on mail yourself, and walked into danger as if it were flat earth; at hand-strokes the chief rebels broke like birds; you carved new lines on the map and opened Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 泰始之末，入參禁旅，任兼軍國，事同顧命。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taishi era he entered to serve in the forbidden guard, his charge embracing army and state, his office like a regent's trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Taishi you entered the palace guard, bearing both army and state on your shoulders, trusted as though at a deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 桂陽負眾，輕問九鼎，裂冠毀冕，拔本塞源，入兵萬乘之國，頓戟象魏之下，烈火焚於王城，飛矢集乎君屋。

translations.literal: Guiyang relied on his masses and lightly questioned the Nine Cauldrons; he tore cap and shattered coronet, uprooted the root and blocked the spring; he brought troops into the realm of ten thousand chariots, halted spears beneath the Elephant Terrace; fierce fire burned in the royal city, flying arrows clustered on the sovereign's roof.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guiyang mustered his crowds and reached for the throne; he defied crown and law, struck at the root of rule; his army poured into the capital, his halberds stood below the royal tower; flame licked the palace, arrows thudded into the emperor's hall.

sentences.zh: 機變儵忽，終古莫二，羣后憂惶，元戎無主。

translations.literal: Fortune shifted in a blink, unmatched through the ages; the lords were anxious and afraid, and the commander-in-chief had no master.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune turned in an eyeblink such as history rarely sees; the great lords trembled, and the host was leaderless.

sentences.zh: 公按劍凝神，則奇謀貫世，秉旄指麾，則懦夫成勇。

translations.literal: When the Duke grasped his sword and gathered his spirit, wondrous stratagems pierced the age; when he took the banner and commanded, cowards became brave.
translations.idiomatic: When you gripped your sword and stilled your mind, stratagems flashed across the age; when you raised the standard, the timid found courage.

sentences.zh: 曾不崇朝，新亭獻捷，信宿之閒，宣陽底定，雲霧廓清，區宇康乂。

translations.literal: In less than a full morning Xinting offered victory; within a night and a day Xuanyang was settled at the base; clouds and mist cleared, and the realm was governed in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Before the morning was spent, Xinting sent up triumph; within two days Xuanyang stood firm; the murk lifted, and the land breathed again.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 皇室多難，釁起戚蕃，邘、晉、應、韓，翻為讎敵，建平失圖，興兵內侮。

translations.literal: The imperial house met many calamities; trouble rose from kin on the frontier; the princes of Gan, Jin, Ying, and Han turned into sworn foes; the Prince of Jianping lost his way and raised arms to insult the court within.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was riven by disaster; rebellion flared among the princes on the marches; Gan, Jin, Ying, and Han became enemies of the throne; Jianping misread the hour and turned his soldiers inward against the court.

sentences.zh: 公又指授六師，義形乎色，役未踰旬，朱方寧晏。

translations.literal: The Duke again directed the six armies; righteousness showed in his face; the campaign had not passed ten days before Zhufang was calm and secure.
translations.idiomatic: You took command of the six hosts, justice written on your brow; in less than ten days Zhufang was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧肆虐，諸夏麋沸，淫刑以逞，誰則無罪，火炎崐岡，玉石俱焚，黔首相悲，朝不謀夕，高祖之業已淪，

translations.literal: Cangwu raged without measure; all Xia seethed like boiling grain; he wielded cruel punishments to his heart's fill—who was without guilt? Fire blazed on Kun's ridge, jade and stone burned together; the black-haired people wept in grief, the court not planning past the morrow; the Founding Emperor's enterprise was already lost,
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Cangwu ran wild; the realm boiled; torture answered his whim and innocence meant nothing; fire on Kun's slopes consumed jade and common stone alike; the people wept, the court could not see tomorrow; the founder's work was already undone,

translations.literal: (Da)
translations.idiomatic: —Da—

sentences.zh: 〔文〕、明之軌誰嗣。

translations.literal: [Wen] and Ming—whose track would succeed?
translations.idiomatic: who would carry on the way of Wen and Ming?

sentences.zh: 公遠稽殷、漢之義，近遵魏、晉之典，猥以眇身，入奉宗祏，七廟清謐，九區反政。

translations.literal: The Duke, looking far to the righteousness of Yin and Han and near to the statutes of Wei and Jin, humbly with his slight person entered to serve the ancestral tablet; the seven temples were pure and still, and the nine regions returned to governance.
translations.idiomatic: You looked back to Yin and Han, took Wei and Jin as your model, and though your person was slight, took up the ancestral shrine; the seven temples grew quiet, and the nine provinces turned again to law.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 袁粲無質，劉秉攜貳，

translations.literal: Yuan Can lacked substance; Liu Bing carried divided loyalty,
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can was hollow at the core; Liu Bing wavered between two masters,

translations.literal: (Tao)
translations.idiomatic: —Tao—

sentences.zh: 〔韞〕、述相扇，成此亂階，醜圖潛構，危機竊發，據有石頭，志犯應、路。

translations.literal: [Yun] and Shu fanned each other, forming this ladder of chaos; ugly plots were woven in secret, crisis broke out by stealth; they held Stone City and aimed at Ying and Lu roads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun and Liu Shu stirred one another on until rebellion climbed its steps; they hid treason, struck by surprise, seized Stone City, and meant to cut the roads to Ying and Lu.

sentences.zh: 公神謀內運，霜鋒外舉，妖沴載澄，國塗悅穆。

translations.literal: The Duke's divine plans worked within; frost blades struck without; demonic ill vapors were cleared away, and the state's path grew glad and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Your counsel moved within like fate; your armies fell like winter steel; the evil air was washed clean, and the realm's way grew bright again.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之苞禍，歲月滋彰，蜂目豺聲，阻兵安忍。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi harbored calamity, which month by month grew plain; with bee eyes and jackal voice he relied on arms and savored cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi nursed treason until none could miss it; his gaze was fierce, his voice was brutal, and he fed on war and ruthlessness.

sentences.zh: 哀彼荊漢，獨為匪民，乃眷西顧，緬同異域。

translations.literal: Alas for Jing and Han—alone made outlaws; he turned his gaze west as though to a foreign land.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Han were pitied as outlaws alone; he looked west as if the throne were already another country.

sentences.zh: 而經綸維始，九伐未申，長惡不悛，遂逞凶逆。

translations.literal: Yet when ordering the realm had only begun, the nine punishments were not yet proclaimed; he clung to long evil without repentance and at last flung himself into fierce treason.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm was still being knit together, the full chastisement had not yet fallen; he would not turn from old crimes and finally rushed headlong into open revolt.

sentences.zh: 驅合姦回，勢過虓虎，朝野憂疑，三軍沮氣。

translations.literal: He drove and gathered the wicked; his force surpassed the tiger; court and countryside were anxious and doubtful, and the three armies' spirit sank.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied every villain; his power outmatched the fiercest beast; court and camp alike wavered, and the army's heart failed.

sentences.zh: 公秉鉞出關，凝威江甸，正情與曒日同亮，明略與秋雲競爽。

translations.literal: The Duke bore the battle-axe beyond the pass, gathered stern might along the Jiang reaches; his upright heart shone with the bright sun, his clear strategy vied with autumn clouds.
translations.idiomatic: You took the axe beyond the passes and let your awe settle over the river lands; your justice matched the noon sun, your design rivaled autumn clarity.

sentences.zh: 至義所感，人百其心，鼖鼓一麾，夏首寧謐，雲梯未舉，魯山剋定。

translations.literal: Where utmost righteousness moved men, a hundred hearts became one; at one beat of the war-drum Xiaoshou was calm and still; before scaling ladders were raised, Lushan was taken and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Where justice led, every man stood as one; one drumbeat and Xiaoshou lay quiet; before the siege engines rose, Lushan had fallen.

sentences.zh: 積年逋誅，一朝顯戮，沮浦安流，章臺順軌。

translations.literal: A rebel long overdue for execution, in one morning paid the price; the Ju shore ran peaceful, Zhangtai returned to the track.
translations.idiomatic: A traitor who had escaped judgment for years died in a single dawn; the Ju flowed easy again, Zhangtai bowed back to law.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too was the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: That too was your deed.

sentences.zh: 公有濟天下之勳，重之以明哲，道庇生民，志匡宇宙，勠力肆心，劬勞王室，自東徂西，靡有寧晏，險阻艱難，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: The Duke had merit that saved the realm, compounded with bright wisdom; his Way sheltered the living, his will squared the universe; he bent all strength to his heart and toiled for the royal house; from east to west there was no calm; hardship and peril he tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: You had saved the world and added wisdom to the deed; you sheltered the people, aimed your will at heaven; you spent yourself for the Song house; from east to west nowhere lay at rest; every hardship of the road you had drunk to the dregs.

sentences.zh: 若乃締構宗稷之勤，造物資始之澤，雲布霧散，光被六幽，弼予一人，永清四海。

translations.literal: As for the toil of founding the altars of state, the grace of the Creator at the beginning—like clouds spread and mist dispersed, his light covered the six dark quarters; he assisted me alone and would forever clear the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: In building the altars anew, in the gift of beginning like rain from heaven, your light reached the farthest shadow; you steadied me alone and promised peace to all beneath the sky.

sentences.zh: 是以秬草騰芳於郊園，景星垂暉於清漢，遐方款關而慕義，荒服重譯而來庭，

translations.literal: Therefore black millet sent forth fragrance in the suburban gardens, and the auspicious star hung its gleam in the clear Han; distant lands knocked at the passes in admiration of righteousness, and wild realms came through double translation to the court,
translations.idiomatic: Black millet sweetened the royal fields, lucky stars burned in the clear sky; far peoples came to the gates in love of right, and barbarian lands sent envoys through double tongues to bow at court,

translations.literal: (Zhu)
translations.idiomatic: —Zhu—

sentences.zh: 〔汪〕哉邈乎！

translations.literal: [How] vast and far!
translations.idiomatic: How vast and far!

sentences.zh: 無得而名焉。

translations.literal: None can name it.
translations.idiomatic: No words can hold it.

sentences.zh: :朕聞疇庸表德，前王盛典，崇樹侯伯，有國攸同。

translations.literal: : I have heard that ranking merit and displaying virtue are the ancient kings' great statutes, and raising feudal lords and princes is the same for all who hold a state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to honor merit and show forth virtue is the ancient kings' highest rite, and to raise feudal lords is the same for every man who receives a state.

sentences.zh: 所以文命成功，玄珪顯錫，姬旦秉哲，曲阜啟蕃，或改玉以弘風，或胙土以宣化，禮絕常班，寵冠羣辟，爰逮桓文，車服異數。

translations.literal: Therefore when civil command succeeded, the dark jade scepter was brightly bestowed; when Ji Dan held wisdom, Qufu opened as a feudatory; some changed jade to spread the wind, some enfeoffed with earth to proclaim transformation—rites set apart from the common rank, favor crowning all peers; down to Duke Huan and Duke Wen, carriage and robes took special numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu finished the work of rule, the dark jade was granted in glory; when the Duke of Zhou held wisdom, Qufu was opened as a fief; some changed jade to widen the wind of rule, some took soil to spread the king's teaching—honors beyond the common roll, favor above every lord; even to Huan and Wen of old, carriage and robe bore special marks.

sentences.zh: 惟公勳業超於先烈，而褒賞闕於舊章，古今之道，何其爽歟？

translations.literal: Only the Duke's achievements surpass the former worthies, yet praise and reward fall short of the old statutes—how sharp the gap between past and present!
translations.idiomatic: Your deeds outshine the heroes of old, yet the rewards of custom do not match—how wide the gulf between then and now!

sentences.zh: 靜言欽歎，良有缺然。

translations.literal: Musing in silence, I admire and sigh; truly something is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I ponder in silence and sigh; plainly something is owed.

sentences.zh: 今進授相國，以青州之齊郡，徐州之梁郡，南徐州之蘭陵、魯郡、琅邪、東海、晉陵、義興，揚州之吳郡、會稽，凡十郡，封公為齊公。

translations.literal: Now I advance and invest you as Chancellor of State, with Qi commandery of Qing Province, Liang commandery of Xu Province, Lanling, Lu, Langye, Donghai, Jinling, and Yixing of South Xu, Wu and Kuaiji of Yang Province—in all ten commanderies—and enfeoff you as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Now I raise you to Chancellor of State and give you ten commanderies: Qi in Qingzhou, Liang in Xuzhou, six commands of South Xu, and Wu and Kuaiji in Yangzhou—and create you Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 錫茲玄土，苴以白茅，定爾邦家，用建冢社。

translations.literal: I bestow this dark earth and wrap it in white thatch; settle your state and house, and thereby establish your ancestral altar.
translations.idiomatic: I grant you the black soil bound in white thatch; fix your state and kin, and found your house shrine.

sentences.zh: 斯實尚父故蕃，世作盟主，紀綱侯甸，率由舊則。

translations.literal: This is truly the old domain of the Martial Father, generation after generation the covenant lord; governing the marches of the feudal lords follows the former rule.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ancient fief of the Grand Duke, for ages the chief of the covenant; to bind the feudal lords is to walk the old path.

sentences.zh: 往者周、邵建國，師保兼任，毛、畢執珪，入作卿士，內外之寄，同規在昔。

translations.literal: In former times the Zhou lords of Zhou and Shao founded states and jointly bore the teacher-and-protector charge; Mao and Bi held the jade tallies and entered as ministers; the trust of inner and outer office matched the pattern of old.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Zhou and Shao founded states and shared tutor and protector alike; Mao and Bi bore the jade tally and became ministers at court; inner trust and outer command followed the same ancient measure.

sentences.zh: 〔今〕命使持節、兼太尉、侍中、中書監、司空、衞將軍、雩都縣開國侯淵授〔公〕相國印綬，齊公璽紱；

translations.literal: [Now] I order Bearer of the Staff, Acting Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Defender of the Realm, Marquis of Yudu county, Yuan to invest [the Duke] with the Chancellor of State's seal and cord and the Duke of Qi's seal and ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: Now I command Bearer of the Staff, Acting Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Defender of the Realm, and Marquis of Yudu, Chu Yuan, to present the Chancellor of State's seal and cord and the Duke of Qi's seal and ribbon;

sentences.zh: 持節、兼司空副、守尚書令僧虔授齊公茅土，金虎符第一至第五左，竹使符第一至第十左。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Acting Vice Minister of Works, Acting Director of the Master of Writing, Sengqian, to invest the Duke of Qi with the feudal earth, gold tiger tallies first through fifth on the left, and bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff, Acting Vice Minister of Works, and Acting Director of the Master of Writing Wang Sengqian to deliver the feudal soil, gold tiger tallies one through five on the left, and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten on the left.

sentences.zh: 相國位總百辟，秩踰三鉉，職以禮移，號隨事革。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State's office heads all the hundred offices; his rank surpasses the three handles; office shifts with ritual, title changes with the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor stands above the hundred offices; his rank exceeds the three highest posts; title and duty move with the rites of the hour.

sentences.zh: 其以相國總百辟，去錄尚書之稱。

translations.literal: Let him as Chancellor of State head the hundred offices and drop the title Recorder of the Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: As Chancellor of State he shall head the hundred offices and lay down the title Recorder of the Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 送所假節、侍中貂蟬、中外都督太傅太尉印綬、竟陵公印策。

translations.literal: Return the lent staff, Palace Attendant's cicada-finch, seals of Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and overall commander within and without, and the patent and seal of Duke of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Send back the lent staff, the palace attendant's fin, the seals of Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and commander inside and outside the realm, and the patent of Duke of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 其驃騎大將軍、揚州牧、南徐州刺史如故。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yang Province, and Inspector of South Xuzhou remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yangzhou, and Inspector of South Xu remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又加公九錫，其敬聽後命：以公秉禮弘律，儀刑區宇，遐邇一體，民無異業，是用錫公大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Moreover I add to the Duke the Nine Bestowals; respectfully hear the following commands: Because the Duke upholds ritual and broadens law, models conduct for the realm, far and near are one body and the people have no alien trades—therefore I bestow a great carriage and a war carriage, each one, and black stallions, two teams of four.
translations.idiomatic: I add the Nine Bestowals; hear what follows with respect: You hold to ritual and widen the law, set the pattern for the realm, and make near and far one household with a single calling—therefore I give a state carriage and a war carriage, and two teams of black stallions.

sentences.zh: 公崇脩南畝，所寶惟穀，王府充實，百姓繁阜，是用錫公袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: The Duke honors and tends the southern fields; what he treasures is grain alone; the royal storehouses are full and the hundred names flourish—therefore I bestow the robe and cap of the twelve symbols, with red slippers besides.
translations.idiomatic: You honor the southern acre and treasure grain above all; the royal granaries are full and the people multiply—therefore I give the twelve-symbol robe and crown, with scarlet shoes.

sentences.zh: 公居身以謙，導物以義，鎔鈞庶品，罔不和悅，是用錫公軒縣之樂，六佾之儛。

translations.literal: The Duke keeps his person in humility and leads things by righteousness; he melts and balances the myriad kinds, and none are not harmonious and glad—therefore I bestow the suspended music of the bell-stands and the six rows of dancers.
translations.idiomatic: You live in humility and lead by righteousness; you temper the myriad things until all are at peace—therefore I give the bell-stand music and dancers in six rows.

sentences.zh: 公翼贊王猷，聲教遠洽，蠻夷竭歡，回首內附，是用錫公朱戶以居。

translations.literal: The Duke wings the king's plans; his voice and teaching reach far; barbarians exhaust their joy and turn their heads to attach within—therefore I bestow vermilion doors to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: You brace the king's design; your teaching runs to the horizon; barbarians rejoice and turn homeward to the throne—therefore I give vermilion gates for your dwelling.

sentences.zh: 公明鑒人倫，澄辨涇渭，官方與能，英乂克舉，是用錫公納陛以登。

translations.literal: The Duke clearly mirrors human relations and clarifies the Jing and Wei; the official ranks employ the able, and heroes are raised—therefore I bestow the ascending ramp of jade.
translations.idiomatic: You mirror human bonds and separate the muddy from the clear; office finds the able and heroes rise—therefore I give the jade ascent to your hall.

sentences.zh: 公保佑皇朝，厲身化下，杜漸防萌，含生夤式，是用錫公虎賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: The Duke protects and blesses the royal house, disciplines his person to transform those below, stops the first sprout and guards against the first bud; all living beings take him as model—therefore I bestow three hundred tiger-guard warriors.
translations.idiomatic: You guard the dynasty, teach by your own conduct, cut evil at the bud; the world takes you as its pattern—therefore I give three hundred tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 公禦宄以刑，禦姦以德，君親無將，將而必誅，是用錫公鈇鉞各一。

translations.literal: The Duke repels the violent by punishment and the treacherous by virtue; for lord and kin there is no "general"—if one becomes a general he must be executed—therefore I bestow an axe and a yue, one each.
translations.idiomatic: You meet violence with punishment and treachery with virtue; no subject may play the general against his prince—and if he does, he dies—therefore I give one battle-axe and one great axe.

sentences.zh: 公鳳舉四維，龍騫八表，威靈所振，異域同文，是用錫公彤弓一，彤矢百，玈弓十，玈矢千。

translations.literal: The Duke rises like the phoenix in the four corners and soars like the dragon through the eight regions; wherever his awing spirit strikes, foreign lands share our script—therefore I bestow one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: You lift like a phoenix to the four quarters and soar like a dragon across the eight directions; where your majesty falls, barbarians learn our writing—therefore I give one red bow, a hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and a thousand black arrows.

sentences.zh: 公明發載懷，肅恭禋祀，孝敬之重，義感靈祇，是用錫公秬鬯一卣，珪瓚副焉。

translations.literal: The Duke at dawn sets forth his cares, reverent and respectful in suburban sacrifice; the weight of filial piety moves the spirits—therefore I bestow one jar of black millet ale, with jade libation vessels besides.
translations.idiomatic: You rise at dawn with the rites upon you, grave in sacrifice to heaven; filial awe moves the gods—therefore I give a jar of sacred ale and jade vessels for libation.

sentences.zh: 齊國置丞相以下，一遵舊式。

translations.literal: In the state of Qi, from Chancellor down, all follows the old form.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, from the chancellor downward, every office follows the former pattern.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go—with respect!
translations.idiomatic: Go—and bear this with reverence!

sentences.zh: 其祗服朕命，經緯乾坤，宏亮洪業，茂昭爾大德，闡揚我高祖之休命。

translations.literal: Reverently accept my command, weave heaven and earth, enlarge and brighten the great enterprise, richly display your great virtue, and spread abroad the fair mandate of our Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Take my command with reverence, bind heaven and earth, widen and illumine the great work, make your virtue shine, and lift high the Founding Emperor's blessed order.

sentences.zh: 太祖三讓，公卿敦勸固請，乃受之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thrice declined; the nobles and ministers pressed him earnestly until he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor refused three times; the court pressed until he yielded.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，下令赦國內殊死以下，今月十五日昧爽以前，一皆原赦，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，賜穀五斛，府州所領，亦同蕩然。

translations.literal: On day dingsi he issued an order pardoning within the realm all crimes below death by special grace; before dawn on the fifteenth of this month all are wholly forgiven; widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves are granted five hu of grain; the prefectures and provinces under his command are likewise cleared.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingsi he decreed amnesty through the realm for all but death sentences; before dawn on the fifteenth of the month every debt of blood and purse was wiped clean; the widowed, orphaned, and destitute received five hu of grain; every district under his rule was cleared the same way.

sentences.zh: 宋帝詔齊公十郡之外，隨宜除用。

translations.literal: The Song emperor decreed that beyond the Duke of Qi's ten commanderies, appointments might be made as fit.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor allowed him to fill posts beyond the ten Qi commanderies as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 以齊國初建，給錢五百萬，布五千匹，絹五千匹。

translations.literal: Because the state of Qi was newly founded, five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and five thousand bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi newly founded, he received five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四月癸酉，詔進齊公爵為王，以豫州之南梁、陳郡、潁川、陳留，南兖州之盱眙、山陽、秦郡、廣陵、海陵、南沛十郡增封。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, day guiyou, an edict advanced the Duke of Qi to king, adding Nanliang, Chen, Yingchuan, and Chenliu of Yu Province and Shuyang, Shanyang, Qin, Guangling, Hailing, and Nanpei of South Yan Province—ten commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, day guiyou, an edict raised the Duke of Qi to king and added ten commands: Nanliang, Chen, Yingchuan, and Chenliu in Yuzhou; Shuyang, Shanyang, Qin, Guangling, Hailing, and Nanpei in South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 使持節、司空、衞將軍褚淵奉策授璽紱，金虎符第一至第五左，竹使符第一至第十左，錫茲玄土，苴白茅，改立王社。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Minister of Works, Defender of the Realm Chu Yuan, bearing the patent, invested him with seal and ribbon, gold tiger tallies first through fifth on the left, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth on the left, bestowed the dark earth, wrapped white thatch, and altered the establishment to a royal altar.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff, Minister of Works, and Defender of the Realm Chu Yuan came with the patent and gave seal and ribbon, gold tiger tallies one through five on the left, bamboo tallies one through ten on the left, the black soil and white thatch, and raised a king's altar in place of the duke's.

sentences.zh: 相國、揚州牧、驃騎大將軍、南徐州刺史如故。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State, Governor of Yang Province, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xuzhou remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State, Governor of Yangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xu stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，命齊王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂儛八佾，設鍾虡宮縣。

translations.literal: On day bingxu he ordered the King of Qi to wear the twelve tassels, raise the Son of Heaven's banners, have guards clear the road when he went out or in, ride the golden-root carriage, drive six horses, keep five seasonal secondary carriages, set yak-tail and cloud-banners, music and dancers in eight rows, and establish bell-stands and palace bells.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingxu he gave the King of Qi the twelve royal tassels, the imperial banners, guards before and behind on the road, the golden-root chariot with six horses, five seasonal spare carriages, yak-tail and cloud pennants, dancers in eight rows, and the bell-stands of a royal court.

sentences.zh: 王世子為太子，王女王孫爵命一如舊儀。

translations.literal: The king's heir was made crown prince; ranks and commands for the king's daughters and grandsons followed the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: His heir became crown prince; titles for daughters and grandsons followed the former rites.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋帝禪位，下詔曰：

translations.literal: On day xinmao the Song emperor abdicated and issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: On day xinmao the Song emperor yielded the throne and proclaimed:

sentences.zh: :惟德動天，玉衡所以載序，窮神知化，億兆所以歸心，用能經緯乾坤，彌綸宇宙，闡揚鴻烈，大庇生民。

translations.literal: : Virtue moves heaven; therefore the jade armillary keeps its sequence. Probing spirit and knowing transformation—therefore the hundred millions turn their hearts. Thus one can weave heaven and earth, fill the universe, spread the great radiance, and broadly shelter the living.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue stirs heaven, and the heavens keep their measure; insight into the unseen turns the hearts of millions; by this one binds heaven and earth, robes the cosmos in order, lifts the great flame of rule, and shelters all who live.

sentences.zh: 晦往明來，積代同軌，前王踵武，世必由之。

translations.literal: Dark departs and bright comes; age after age shares one track; former kings tread martial steps—each generation must pass this way.
translations.idiomatic: Night yields to day as age follows age; every king who came before walked this road of transfer; none may escape the path.

sentences.zh: 宋德湮微，昏毀相襲，景和騁悖於前，元徽肆虐於後，三光再霾，七廟將墜，璇極委馭，含識知泯，我文、武之祚，眇焉如綴。

translations.literal: Song virtue sank and grew slight; blindness and ruin followed in turn; Jinghe ran wild in the first, Yuanhui raged in the last; the three luminaries were dimmed twice, the seven temples were about to fall; the pole star yielded the chariot, and conscious beings knew extinction; our Wen and Wu's fortune hung by a thread, tiny as a trailing cord.
translations.idiomatic: Song's mandate thinned; folly and ruin came hand in hand; Jinghe's madness led, Yuanhui's cruelty followed; sun, moon, and stars were veiled again, the seven temples tottered; the throne's pivot slipped away, and the world seemed already dead; the fortune Wen and Wu left hung by a thread no thicker than a single strand.

sentences.zh: 靜惟此紊，夕惕疚心。

translations.literal: Musing in silence on this disorder, evening and morning I am pierced with guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I ponder this chaos in silence and feel guilt at every turn of the day.

sentences.zh: :相國齊王，天誕叡聖，河嶽炳靈，拯傾提危，澄氛靜亂，匡濟艱難，功均造物。

translations.literal: : The Chancellor of State, King of Qi, was born of heaven's keen sagacity; river and mountain burned with spirit; he righted the leaning and lifted the endangered, cleared vapors and stilled disorder, aided through hardship, his merit equal to the Creator.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State, King of Qi, was born with heaven's clarity; rivers and peaks shone in his making; he propped the tottering throne, stilled the storm, bore the realm through peril, and his merit matched the work of heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 宏謀霜照，祕筭雲回，旌旆所臨，一麾必捷，英風所拂，無思不偃，表裏清夷，遐邇寧謐。

translations.literal: His grand design frost-bright, his secret reckonings cloud-swift; wherever his banners pointed, one wave brought victory; wherever his heroic wind brushed, none who thought did not bow; inner and outer were pure, far and near were calm.
translations.idiomatic: His plans were bright as frost, his hidden counts swift as cloud; where his banners turned, one gesture won the field; where his spirit passed, every will bent; within and without grew clear, near and far lay still.

sentences.zh: 既而光啟憲章，弘宣禮教，姦宄之類，覩隆威而隔情，慕善之儔，仰徽猷而增厲。

translations.literal: Thereafter he brightly opened the statutes, broadly proclaimed ritual teaching; the class of traitors, seeing lofty awe, held their feelings apart; those who loved good, looking up to fine doctrine, grew the more stern.
translations.idiomatic: Then he opened the laws in glory and spread ritual abroad; villains, seeing his majesty, shrank from their designs; men who loved the good, lifting their eyes to his teaching, strove the harder.

sentences.zh: 道邁於重華，勳超乎文命，蕩蕩乎無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: His Way surpassed Chonghua, his merit exceeded Wenming; vast and boundless—there was nothing by which to name him.
translations.idiomatic: His Way outran Shun, his merit outran Yu; so vast that no praise could compass him.

sentences.zh: 是以辮髮左衽之酋，款關請吏，木衣卉服之長，航海來庭，豈惟肅慎獻楛，越

translations.literal: Therefore chiefs with braided hair and left lapels came to the passes in homage and asked for officials; elders in bark robes and plant garments sailed the seas to court—is it only Sushen presenting hazel bows, or Yue
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs with braided hair and left lapels came to the gates to swear fealty; lords in bark and leaves crossed the sea to court—was it only Sushen with their hazel bows, or Yue

sentences.zh: 〔裳〕薦翬而已哉。

translations.literal: [裳] presenting pheasant plumes—and no more?
translations.idiomatic: of Yue with their pheasant plumes, and nothing more?

sentences.zh: 故四奧載宅，六府克和，川陸効珍，禎祥鱗集，卿煙玉露，旦夕揚藻，嘉穟芝英，晷刻呈茂。

translations.literal: Thus the four quarters bore their dwellings, the six treasuries were in harmony, land and water offered their treasures, auspicious signs gathered thick as scales, ministerial mist and jade dew rose morning and evening, fine grain and spirit fungus showed their glory at every turn of the sundial.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters held their homes, the six treasuries chimed, river and road yielded wonders, omens crowded in, courtly mist and jade dew lifted at dawn and dusk, and lucky grain and spirit fungus flourished hour by hour.

sentences.zh: 革運斯炳，代終彌亮，負扆握樞，允歸明哲，固以獄訟去宋，謳歌適齊。

translations.literal: The change of mandate blazed forth; at an age's end it shone the brighter; leaning on the screen and holding the pivot—truly it returned to the wise and clear; thus lawsuits left Song and songs of praise turned toward Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate turned and flared; as the dynasty ended, light gathered on the throne; the screen and the pivot belonged at last to wisdom—so the people's suits quit Song and their songs ran toward Qi.

sentences.zh: :昔金政既淪，水德締構，天之曆數，皎焉攸徵。

translations.literal: : Of old the Metal phase had sunk, and the Water phase founded the structure; Heaven's calendar was bright where it was signified.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the Metal reign had fallen and the Water reign was being woven; Heaven's count was plain for all to read.

sentences.zh: 朕雖寡昧，闇于大道，稽覽隆替，為日已久，敢忘列代遺則，人神至願乎？

translations.literal: Though I am shallow and dull, dark to the Great Way, I have long pondered rise and fall—how dare I forget the precedents of former ages or the utmost wish of men and spirits?
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and small, blind to the Great Way, yet I have weighed fortune's turns for years—how could I forget the models of the past or what men and gods desire?

sentences.zh: 便遜位別宮，敬禪于齊，一依唐虞、魏晉故事。

translations.literal: I shall at once yield the throne and retire to a separate palace, reverently abdicating to Qi, wholly following the precedents of Tang-Yao, Yu-Shun, Wei, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I will yield the throne at once and withdraw to the eastern lodge, abdicating in full reverence to Qi after the manner of Yao, Shun, Wei, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 是日宋帝遜于東邸，備羽儀，乘畫輪車，出東掖門，問今日何不奏鼓吹，左右莫有答者。

translations.literal: That day the Song emperor yielded at the Eastern Lodge; with full feathered regalia he rode the painted wheel carriage out the Eastern Flank Gate and asked, "Why is no drum-and-pipe music played today?"—none on his left or right answered.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Song emperor left for the Eastern Lodge in full regalia, rode the painted carriage out the Eastern Flank Gate, and asked why no drums and pipes sounded today; no one beside him spoke.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，策命齊王曰：

translations.literal: On day renchen an edict invested the King of Qi, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On day renchen the investiture edict to the King of Qi read:

sentences.zh: :伊太古初陳，萬物紛綸，開耀靈以鑑品物，立元后以馭蒸人。

translations.literal: : In the first unfolding of utmost antiquity the myriad things were tangled in skeins; the Radiant Spirit was opened to mirror the classes of things, and the primordial consort was set up to govern the teeming people.
translations.idiomatic: At the first dawn of time the ten thousand things were chaos; the bright spirit was opened to judge all kinds, and the first queen was raised to rule the people.

sentences.zh: 若夫容成、大庭之世，宓羲、五龍之辰，靡得而詳焉。

translations.literal: As for the age of Rongcheng and Great Court, the time of Fuxi and the Five Dragons—none can be told in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Of Rongcheng, of Great Court, of Fuxi and the Five Dragons—no one can speak them whole.

sentences.zh: 自軒黃以降，墳素所紀，略可言者，莫崇乎堯舜。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor downward, what the buried silks record and may be spoken of in brief—none is more honored than Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor on, what the old books allow us to name—nothing stands higher than Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 披金繩而握天鏡，開玉匣而總地維，德之休明，宸居靈極。

translations.literal: They spread the golden cord and grasped the heavenly mirror, opened the jade casket and gathered the earth's warp; virtue luminous and resting, the purple dwelling at the numinous pole.
translations.idiomatic: They took up the golden rope and the sky's mirror, opened the jade box and held the earth's warp; their virtue shone, and the throne stood at the pole.

sentences.zh: 期運有終，歸禪與能。

translations.literal: When the allotted season had its end, they returned the abdication to the able.
translations.idiomatic: When their term was done, they yielded the throne to worthier men.

sentences.zh: 所以大唐遜位，䜎然興歌，有虞揖讓，卿雲發采。

translations.literal: Therefore Great Tang yielded the throne and songs rose in sudden joy; You of Yu bowed and yielded, and auspicious clouds flashed their colors.
translations.idiomatic: So Great Tang abdicated and the people burst into song; Shun bowed and yielded, and lucky clouds burned bright.

sentences.zh: 亮符命之攸臻，坦至公以成務，懷生載懌，靈祇効祉，遺風餘烈，光被無垠。
