translations.literal: Bright where mandate and fortune drew near, level in utmost fairness to complete the task—the living were laden with joy, spirits and earth offered blessing; the lingering wind and remaining blaze shone without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs gathered, public heart was open, all under heaven rejoiced, gods and earth sent blessing, and the fame of those days still lights the horizon.

sentences.zh: 漢魏因循，弗敢失墜，爰逮晉氏，亦遵前儀。

translations.literal: Han and Wei followed in succession and did not dare let the rite fall; reaching the House of Jin, they too kept the former ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei followed one another and never dropped the rite; Jin too held to the old way.

sentences.zh: 惟我祖宗英叡，勳格幽顯，從天人而齊七政，凝至德而撫四維。

translations.literal: Our ancestors were heroic and keen; their merit touched hidden and manifest; aligning the seven regulators with Heaven and man, they condensed utmost virtue and soothed the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears were keen and bright; their merit reached ghost and world; they matched heaven and earth in the seven regulators and gathered utmost virtue to calm the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 末葉不造，仍世多故，

translations.literal: The last branch was unblessed; age after age met with many troubles,
translations.idiomatic: The last branches were ill-fated; generation after generation knew disaster,

sentences.zh: （難滅星謀）

translations.literal: (hard-to-extinguish star plots)
translations.idiomatic: —[eclipses and falling stars]—

sentences.zh: 〔日蝕星隕〕，山淪川竭。

translations.literal: [eclipses and falling stars], mountains collapsed and rivers ran dry.
translations.idiomatic: eclipses darkened the sky and stars fell, mountains sank and rivers failed.

sentences.zh: :惟王聖哲淵明，榮鏡㝢宙，體望日之威，資就雲之澤，臨下以簡，御眾以寬，仁育羣生，義征不譓，國塗荐阻，弘五慮而乂寧，皇緒將湮，秉六術以匡濟。

translations.literal: : Only the King is sage and profound, a glorious mirror to the universe; he embodies the awe of the sun on the horizon and draws on the moisture of rain-bearing clouds; he oversees those below with simplicity and rules the multitude with breadth; with benevolence he nurtures all life, with righteousness he punishes the unrepentant; when the state's road was repeatedly blocked, he spread five counsels and brought peace; when the imperial line was near extinction, he wielded six arts and righted the peril.
translations.idiomatic: The King alone is deep and wise, a bright mirror to all under heaven; he has the sun's majesty and the cloud's rain; simple with those below, broad with the masses, he feeds the people with benevolence and chastises the stubborn with righteousness; when the realm was choked he opened five counsels and made it quiet, and when the royal thread was drowning he took up six arts and saved it.

sentences.zh: 及至權臣內侮，蕃屏陵上，兵革雲翔，萬邦震駭，裁之以武風，綏之以文化，遐邇清夷，表裏肅穆。

translations.literal: When powerful ministers insulted within and the screen-lords bullied above, weapons and armor flew like clouds and ten thousand states trembled in fear—he cut them with the martial wind and soothed them with civil transformation; far and near were cleared, within and without were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers preyed within and the imperial kin bullied the throne, war rose like storm clouds and every state shook—he struck with the sword and soothed with culture until near and far were clean and court and country stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 戢琱戈而事黼黻，委旌門而恭儒館，聲化遠洎，荒服無塵，殊類同規，華戎一揆。

translations.literal: He stowed the carved halberds and turned to brocade and embroidery, left the banner gate and honored the Confucian hall; his voice and transforming power reached far, the wild domains knew no dust, unlike kinds shared one measure, Hua and Rong were of a single rule.
translations.idiomatic: He sheathed the weapons and took up brocade, left the camp gate for the school; his fame ran to the ends of the earth, the wild marches went quiet, barbarian and Chinese walked one path.

sentences.zh: 是以五光來儀於軒庭，九穗含芳於郊牧。

translations.literal: Therefore the five lights came to court in the Xuan courtyard, and nine ears of grain bore fragrance in the suburban pastures.
translations.idiomatic: So the five-colored lights appeared in the hall, and nine-headed grain bloomed fragrant in the fields.

sentences.zh: 象緯昭澈，布新之符已顯，圖讖彪炳，受終之義既彰。

translations.literal: The astral signs were bright and clear; the omen of renewal was already plain; charts and prophecies blazed forth, and the meaning of receiving the end was already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs shone clear, the mark of a new age was plain, omens and prophecies flared, and the mandate to receive the succession stood open.

sentences.zh: 靈祇乃眷，兆民引領。

translations.literal: Spirits and earth then looked with favor; the million people craned their necks.
translations.idiomatic: Gods and earth turned their gaze; the people stretched their necks to see.

sentences.zh: 朕聞至道深微，惟人是弘，天命無常，惟德是與。

translations.literal: I have heard that the utmost Way is deep and subtle—only in men is it magnified; the Mandate of Heaven is without constancy—only virtue is granted.
translations.idiomatic: The highest Way is deep and fine, and lives only in men; Heaven's mandate does not stay—only virtue keeps it.

sentences.zh: 所以仰鑒玄情，俯察羣望，敬禪神器，授帝位于爾躬。

translations.literal: Therefore, looking up to mirror the dark mystery and looking down to examine the multitude's hopes, I reverently abdicate the sacred vessel and confer the imperial seat upon your person.
translations.idiomatic: So, reading heaven above and the people's longing below, I yield the sacred throne and set the imperial seat on you.

sentences.zh: 四海困窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: Within the four seas all is exhausted; Heaven's blessing has reached its end.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas are spent; Heaven's tenure is finished.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 王其允執厥中，儀刑前式，以副率土之欣望。

translations.literal: O King, truly hold the mean, take the former kings as your model, and answer the joyful hope of all within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: King, hold the middle way, follow the ancient kings, and meet the joy of all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 命司裘而謁蒼昊，奏雲門而升圓丘，時膺大禮，永保洪業，豈不盛歟！

translations.literal: Charge the Master of Garments to pay homage to the azure Heaven, perform the Cloud Gate and ascend the Round Mound; in season receive the great rites and forever preserve the great enterprise—how is this not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Send the Master of Robes to worship Heaven, play the Cloud Gate and climb the Round Mound; take the great rites in their season and keep the great work forever—what glory could exceed this!

sentences.zh: 再命璽書曰：

translations.literal: Again an edict with the imperial seal read:
translations.idiomatic: A second letter under the imperial seal said:

sentences.zh: :皇帝敬問相國齊王。

translations.literal: : The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Chancellor of State, King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor respectfully addresses the Chancellor of State, King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 大道之行，與三代之英，朕雖闇昧，而有志焉。

translations.literal: When the Great Way was practiced, and the worthies of the Three Dynasties—though I am dark and dull, I have the will for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Way once walked the earth, and the heroes of the Three Dynasties shone—dim as I am, I have wished for that.

sentences.zh: 夫昏明相襲，晷景之恆度，春秋遞運，時歲之常序。

translations.literal: Dark and bright succeed one another—the constant measure of the sundial's shadow; spring and autumn pass in turn—the regular order of the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day take turns—that is the sundial's law; spring and autumn wheel on—that is the year's order.

sentences.zh: 求諸天數，猶且隆替，矧伊在人，能無終謝。

translations.literal: Seek it in Heaven's numbers and there is still rise and fall—how much more among men can there be no final decline?
translations.idiomatic: Even in Heaven's count there is waxing and waning—how could men escape their end?

sentences.zh: 是故勛華弘風於上葉，漢魏垂式於後昆。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao and Shun spread their wind in the upper branches, and Han and Wei left their pattern to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: So Yao and Shun set the tone in the high age, and Han and Wei left a model for those who came after.

sentences.zh: :昔我高祖，欽明文思，振民育德，皇靈眷命，奄有四海。

translations.literal: : Of old our High Ancestor was reverent, bright, cultured, and thoughtful; he stirred the people and nurtured virtue; the august spirit looked with favor and suddenly held the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Our High Ancestor was reverent, bright, learned, and deep; he roused the people and fed virtue until the sacred spirit smiled and the four seas were his.

sentences.zh: 晚世多難，姦宄寔繁，鼖鼓宵聞，元戎旦警，億兆夷人，啟處靡厝。

translations.literal: The late age met many hardships; traitors and villains were indeed numerous; war drums sounded through the night, the grand army was on alert at dawn; the hundred million common folk had no place to rest from rising to lying down.
translations.idiomatic: The late reign knew one disaster after another; villains swarmed; drums beat all night and the host was armed at dawn; millions of people could not find rest from dawn to dark.

sentences.zh: 加以嗣君荒怠，敷虐萬方，神鼎將遷，寶策無主，實賴英聖，匡濟艱危。

translations.literal: Added to this, the succeeding ruler was wild and slack, spreading cruelty through the ten thousand regions; the sacred tripod was about to move, the precious registers had no master—truly we relied on heroic sagacity to right the peril.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was idle and cruel and scourged the realm; the sacred vessel was shifting and the registers had no lord—we lived only by a hero's hand in the storm.

sentences.zh: 惟王體天則地，舍弘光大，明竝日月，惠均雲雨。

translations.literal: Only the King models Heaven and earth, is magnanimous and bright, his clarity matches sun and moon, his grace equals cloud and rain.
translations.idiomatic: The King alone takes heaven and earth as his pattern, vast and bright; his light is the sun and moon, his kindness is cloud and rain.

sentences.zh: 國步斯梗，則稜威外發，王猷不造，則淵謨內昭。

translations.literal: When the state's step was blocked, then stern awe flashed outward; when the royal plan was unformed, then deep counsel shone within.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm stumbled, his stern light struck outward; when the royal design was unclear, his deep counsel lit the court within.

sentences.zh: 重構閩、吳，再寧淮、濟，靜九江之洪波，卷海沂之氛沴，放斥凶昧，存我宗祀，舊物惟新，王光改照。

translations.literal: He rebuilt Min and Wu, again quieted Huai and Ji, stilled the great waves of the Nine Rivers, rolled up the miasma of the sea shores, drove off the vicious and blind, preserved our ancestral sacrifices; old things were made new, the King's radiance changed its illumination.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt Min and Wu, stilled Huai and Ji again, calmed the Jiujiang floods, swept the coastal plague, cast out the wicked, kept our altars burning, made the old new, and turned the King's light across the land.

sentences.zh: 逮至寵臣裂冠，則裁以廟略，荊漢反噬，則震以雷霆。

translations.literal: When favored ministers tore the crown, then he cut them with the temple strategy; when Jing and Han turned to bite, then he shook them with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: When court favorites broke rank, he cut them with statecraft; when Jing and Han rose against him, he answered with thunder.

sentences.zh: 麾旆所臨，風行草靡，神筭所指，龍舉雲屬。

translations.literal: Where his banners and staffs reached, the wind blew and grass bent; where his divine reckoning pointed, dragons rose and clouds gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Where his banners went, grass bent in the wind; where his strategy pointed, hosts rose like dragons on clouds.

sentences.zh: 諸夏廓清，戎翟思韙，興文偃武，闡揚洪烈。

translations.literal: The many Xia were cleared, the Rong and Di thought of goodness; he raised culture and laid war aside, spreading the great blaze.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was cleared, the barbarians turned to right; he raised learning and stilled arms and widened the great flame.

sentences.zh: 明保沖昧，翺翔禮樂之場，撫柔黔首，咸

translations.literal: Brightly guarding his modest dullness, he soared in the field of ritual and music; soothing and softening the black-haired people, all
translations.idiomatic: Guarding his own modesty, he moved in ritual and music; gentling the people, all

translations.literal: (crossed)
translations.idiomatic: —[ascended]—

sentences.zh: 〔躋〕仁壽之域。

translations.literal: [ascended] the realm of benevolent longevity.
translations.idiomatic: ascended to the land of benevolent long life.

sentences.zh: 自霜露所墜，星辰所經，正朔不通，人跡罕至者，莫不踰山越海，北面稱蕃，款關重譯，脩其職貢。

translations.literal: From where frost and dew fall to where the stars pass, wherever the calendar did not reach and human tracks were rare—none failed to cross mountains and seas, turn north and call themselves vassals, come to the passes through repeated interpreters, and repair their tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the reach of frost to the track of stars, wherever the calendar had not run and feet seldom walked—none failed to cross sea and mountain, turn north as vassals, come through many tongues to the gate, and keep their tribute.

sentences.zh: 是以禎祥發采，左史載其奇，玄象垂文，保章審其度，鳳書表肆類之運，龍圖顯班瑞之期。

translations.literal: Therefore auspicious signs flashed their colors; the Left Historian recorded their marvels; dark images hung their writing; the Keeper of Omens examined their measures; the phoenix book showed the fortune of the four classes; the dragon chart revealed the season of distributed auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Omens flared, the Left Historian wrote the wonder, heaven's signs wrote their text, the omen officer judged their degree, the phoenix book marked the age of the peoples, and the dragon chart showed the hour of grace.

sentences.zh: 重以珠衡日角，神姿特挺，君人之義，在事必彰。

translations.literal: Added to this, pearl balance and sun corner—his divine bearing outstanding; the meaning of a ruler over men, in affairs must be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: And with pearl brow and sun corner, his godlike form stood apart; a king's bearing shows itself in every deed.

sentences.zh: 書不云乎，「皇天無親，惟德是輔」。

translations.literal: Does the Book not say, "August Heaven is not partial—only virtue is assisted"?
translations.idiomatic: The Book says: "High Heaven has no favorites—it helps only the virtuous."

sentences.zh: 民心無常，惟惠之懷。

translations.literal: The people's hearts are without constancy—only kindness is what they cherish.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts shift; only grace wins them.

sentences.zh: 神祇之眷如彼，蒼生之願如此。

translations.literal: The favor of spirits and earth was like that; the wish of the black-haired people was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Gods and earth favored him so; the people wished it so.

sentences.zh: 笙管變聲，鍾石改調。

translations.literal: Pipes and flutes changed their notes; bells and stones altered their tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes and bells were already changing their pitch.

sentences.zh: 朕所以擁琁持衡，傾佇明哲。

translations.literal: Therefore I hold the jade scepter and the balance, leaning in expectation of the wise and clear.
translations.idiomatic: So I hold the jade and the scale and wait, bowed toward wisdom.

sentences.zh: :昔金德既淪，而傳祚于我有宋，曆數告終，寔在茲日，亦以水德而傳于齊。

translations.literal: : Of old the Metal virtue had sunk, and the succession passed to our Song; the calendar announced its end—truly it is on this day—and likewise by Water virtue it passes to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Metal reign fell, the line came to our Song; the count ends today and by Water's turn passes to Qi.

sentences.zh: 式遵前典，廣詢羣議，王公卿士，咸曰惟宜。

translations.literal: Following the former canon, I have broadly consulted the multitude of counsels; kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars all say it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: By the old rite I asked far and wide; princes and ministers alike said it must be done.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節、兼太保、侍中、中書監、司空、衞將軍、雩都縣侯淵，兼太尉、守尚書令僧虔奉皇帝璽綬，受終之禮，一依唐虞故事。

translations.literal: Now I send the envoy bearing the staff, Concurrent Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, General of the Guard, Marquis of Yudu county Chu Yuan, and Concurrent Grand Commandant, Acting Director of the Master of Writing Wang Sengqian to present the imperial seal and cord and perform the rite of receiving the end, wholly following the Tang-Yao precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I now send Staff-Bearer Chu Yuan, Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, Minister of Works, Guard General, and Marquis of Yudu, with Grand Commandant Wang Sengqian, Acting Master of Writing, to deliver the imperial seal and cord and complete the abdication rite as in the time of Yao.

sentences.zh: 王其允副幽明，時登元后，寵綏八表，以酬昊天之休命。

translations.literal: O King, truly answer to hidden and manifest, take the primordial consort in season, cherish and soothe the eight regions, and repay the august Heaven's fine command.
translations.idiomatic: King, answer heaven and earth, mount the throne in season, soothe the eight directions, and repay Heaven's bright mandate.

sentences.zh: 太祖三辭，宋帝王公以下固請。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor declined three times; the Song emperor, kings, dukes, and all below pressed him firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor refused three times; the Song emperor and the whole court pressed until he could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 兼太史令、將作匠陳文建奏符命曰：「六，亢位也。

translations.literal: Concurrent Grand Astrologer and Master of Works Chen Wenjian memorialized on the mandate-token, saying: "Six is the position of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer and Master of Works Chen Wenjian submitted on the heavenly signs: "Six is the Kang position.

sentences.zh: 後漢自建武至建安二十五年，一百九十六年而禪魏；

translations.literal: Later Han from Jianwu to the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an—one hundred ninety-six years—and abdicated to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Later Han from Jianwu to Jian'an twenty-five: one hundred ninety-six years, then abdication to Wei;

sentences.zh: 〔魏〕自黃初至咸熙二年，四十六年而禪晉；

translations.literal: [Wei] from Huangchu to the second year of Xianxi—forty-six years—and abdicated to Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Wei from Huangchu to Xianxi two: forty-six years, then abdication to Jin;

sentences.zh: 晉自太始至元熙二年，一百五十六年而禪宋；

translations.literal: Jin from Taishi to the second year of Yuanxi—one hundred fifty-six years—and abdicated to Song;
translations.idiomatic: Jin from Taishi to Yuanxi two: one hundred fifty-six years, then abdication to Song;

sentences.zh: 宋自永初元年至昇明三年，凡六十年：咸以六終六受。

translations.literal: Song from the first year of Yongchu to the third year of Shengming—sixty years in all: all ended in six and received in six.
translations.idiomatic: Song from Yongchu one to Shengming three: sixty years in all—each dynasty ended in six and received in six.

sentences.zh: 六，亢位也。

translations.literal: Six is the position of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Six is the Kang position.

sentences.zh: 驗往揆今，若斯昭著。

translations.literal: Testing the past and measuring the present, it is thus bright and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present alike show it plain.

sentences.zh: 敢以職任，備陳管穴。

translations.literal: I venture, in duty of office, to set forth this narrow glimpse from the tube.
translations.idiomatic: In my office I dare offer this small glimpse through the tube.

sentences.zh: 伏願順天時，膺符瑞。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that you follow Heaven's season and receive the mandate-tokens.
translations.idiomatic: I bow and ask you to follow Heaven's hour and take the signs.

sentences.zh: 」二朝百辟又固請。

translations.literal: " The hundred ministers of the two courts again pressed firmly.
translations.idiomatic: " Then the ministers of both courts pressed again.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射王儉奏：「被宋詔遜位。

translations.literal: Director of the Master of Writing, Right Vice Director Wang Jian memorialized: "We have received the Song edict to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director of the Master of Writing Wang Jian submitted: "We have received the Song order to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜剋日輿駕受禪，撰立儀注。

translations.literal: Your ministers have deliberated together and deem that on an appointed day Your Majesty should mount the carriage and receive the abdication, and that the ritual regulations should be drafted and set.
translations.idiomatic: We have met and hold that the abdication should be set for a fixed day, with rites drafted and established.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃許焉。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founding Emperor then agreed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：案太一九宮占推漢高五年，太一在四宮，主人與客俱得吉，計先舉事者勝，是歲高祖破楚。

translations.literal: The historian says: Examining the Taiyi Nine Palaces prognostication—pushing to the fifth year of Han Gaozu, Taiyi was in the fourth palace; host and guest both obtained auspice; reckoning that the side which raised affairs first would win—in that year Gaozu defeated Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: On the Taiyi Nine Palaces chart, in Gaozu's fifth year Taiyi stood in the fourth palace; host and guest were both lucky, and whoever moved first would win—that year Gaozu broke Chu.

sentences.zh: 晉元興二年，太一在七宮，太一為帝，天目為輔佐，迫脅太一，是年安帝為桓玄所逼出宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxing of Jin, Taiyi was in the seventh palace; Taiyi was the emperor, Tianmu was the assistant, pressing and threatening Taiyi—in that year Emperor An was forced by Huan Xuan to leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Yuanxing two: Taiyi in the seventh palace; Taiyi as emperor, Tianmu as aide, pressing Taiyi—that year Emperor An was driven from the palace by Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 大將在一宮，參相在三宮，格太一。

translations.literal: The Great General was in the first palace, the Participating Minister in the third palace, checking Taiyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Great General stood in the first palace, the Participating Minister in the third, blocking Taiyi.

sentences.zh: 經言格者，已立政事，上下格之，不利有為，安居之世，不利舉動。

translations.literal: The classic says that to check means affairs are already established and above and below block them—unfavorable to action; in a time of settled peace, unfavorable to movement.
translations.idiomatic: The text says checking means government is fixed and all sides resist it—bad for action; in quiet times, bad for stirring.

sentences.zh: 元興三年，太一在七宮，宋武破桓玄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing, Taiyi was in the seventh palace; Song Wu defeated Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing three: Taiyi in the seventh palace; Song Wu broke Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，太一在六宮，不利有為，徐、傅廢營陽王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia, Taiyi was in the sixth palace—unfavorable to action; Xu and Fu deposed Prince Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia one: Taiyi in the sixth palace, ill for action; Xu and Fu deposed Prince Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，太一在八宮，關囚惡歲，大小將皆不得立，其年到彥之北伐，初勝後敗，客主俱不利。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Taiyi was in the eighth palace—a year of imprisonment and evil; neither Great nor Small General could stand; that year Dao Yanzhi marched north, winning at first and losing later; guest and host were both harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven: Taiyi in the eighth palace, a caged, evil year; neither general could hold; that year Dao Yanzhi's northern campaign won, then lost; both sides suffered.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太一在二宮，客主俱不利，是歲氐楊難當寇梁、益，來年仇池破。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Taiyi was in the second palace; guest and host were both harmed—that year the Di chieftain Yang Nandang raided Liang and Yi; the next year Qiu Chi fell.
translations.idiomatic: Year eighteen: Taiyi in the second palace, both sides hurt; Yang Nandang of the Di raided Liang and Yi; Qiu Chi fell the year after.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大小將皆見關不立，凶，其年裴方明伐仇池，剋百頃，明年失之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Great and Small Generals both saw imprisonment and could not stand—inauspicious; that year Pei Fangming attacked Qiu Chi, took a hundred qing, and lost it the next year.
translations.idiomatic: Year nineteen: both generals blocked and could not stand—ill luck; Pei Fangming took Qiu Chi and a hundred qing, then lost it all the next year.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，太一在二宮，為大小將奄擊之，其年景和廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi, Taiyi was in the second palace, attacked and smothered by Great and Small Generals; that year Jinghe was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi one: Taiyi in the second palace, crushed by both generals; that year Emperor Jinghe was deposed.

sentences.zh: 二年，太一在三宮，不利先起，主人勝，其年晉安王子勛反。

translations.literal: In the second year, Taiyi was in the third palace—unfavorable to moving first, the host wins; that year Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Year two: Taiyi in the third palace, bad to strike first, the host wins; Prince Zixun of Jin'an rose that year.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，太一在六宮，先起敗，是歲桂陽王休範反，竝伏誅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, Taiyi was in the sixth palace—whoever moved first was defeated; that year Prince Guiyang Huo Fan rebelled, and both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhui two: Taiyi in the sixth palace, first mover lost; Prince Guiyang Huo Fan rebelled and was killed with his party.

sentences.zh: 四年，太一在七宮，先起者客，西北走，其年建平王景素敗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Taiyi was in the seventh palace—whoever moved first was the guest and fled northwest; that year Prince Jianping Jing Su was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Year four: Taiyi in the seventh palace, first mover was guest and fled northwest; Prince Jianping Jing Su was ruined that year.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，太一在七宮，不利為客，安居之世，舉事為主人，應發為客，袁粲、沈攸之等反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming, Taiyi was in the seventh palace—unfavorable to be guest; in a time of settled peace, to raise affairs is to be host; to respond when roused is to be guest; Yuan Can, Shen Youzhi, and others rebelled and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming one: Taiyi in the seventh palace, ill to be guest; in peace, the mover is host, the responder guest; Yuan Can, Shen Youzhi, and the rest rose and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 是歲太一在杜門，臨八宮，宋帝禪位，不利為客，安居之世，舉事為主人，禪代之應也。

translations.literal: That year Taiyi was at Du Gate, facing the eighth palace; the Song emperor abdicated—unfavorable to be guest; in a time of settled peace, to raise affairs is to be host—the response of abdication.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taiyi stood at Du Gate over the eighth palace; the Song emperor abdicated—ill to be guest, good for the host who holds peace; that was the omen of transfer.
